issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`extensions/microsoft-foundry/shared.ts` `resolveFoundryModelTokenLimits` (~line 228) grants a 1M-token context window / 128k maxTokens whenever `supportsClaudeAdaptiveThinking({ id })` is true. Since #196459, that helper intentionally answers **true for unknown Claude ids** (adaptive thinking stays on for unreleased models). A future Claude deployed in Foundry but not yet listed in OpenClaw's model catalog (e.g. `claude-opus-6`) therefore gets configured with `contextWindow: 1_000_000` / `maxTokens: 128_000` even though its real window is unknown and likely smaller. This is the same class of defect #196459 fixed for the anthropic route: unknown models must not be assumed to have a 1M window.

## Why

The 1M-context check should use the helper whose semantics are "unknown → false": `supportsClaude1MContext` (= `isReleasedAdaptiveClaudeGeneration`, unknown → false, defined in `packages/llm-core/src/model-contracts/anthropic.ts`). It is exported from the same public barrel (`openclaw/plugin-sdk/provider-model-shared`) the file already imports `supportsClaudeAdaptiveThinking` from, so the fix is a one-line swap plus one import.

The thinking-support check at `resolveFoundryModelCapabilities` (~line 375) intentionally keeps `supportsClaudeAdaptiveThinking` — an unknown Claude should be assumed to support thinking — and is left untouched.

## User Impact

A Foundry user who deploys a future/unlisted Claude model gets a model configured with `contextWindow: 1_000_000` and `maxTokens: 128_000`. If the real model's window is smaller, sessions are not compacted at the real limit and the request fails with `context_length_exceeded`/400, or the 128k maxTokens is rejected. After the fix, unknown Claude models fall back to the conservative 128k/16k limits instead of being over-provisioned.

## Evidence

Pure-function vitest lane (producer-chain; the remote host cannot run a Gateway/e2e — kernel lacks openat2). New table row `["claude-opus-6", "anthropic-messages", "api-key", 128_000, 16_384]` in `extensions/microsoft-foundry/shared.test.ts`.

- **Red (base `ac7e941722a` + new test, old source)**: `1 failed | 26 passed` — `claude-opus-6` got `contextWindow: 1000000` / `maxTokens: 128000`.
- **Green (head `60a848d27f9` + new source)**: `27 passed` — `claude-opus-6` → `128000/16384`; known models unchanged (`claude-opus-5`/`claude-sonnet-4.6` still 1M/128k, `claude-sonnet-4.5` 200k/64k, `claude-opus-4.1` 200k/32k).
- Full foundry extension suite on head: **5 files / 98 tests pass**, no regression.

### Review follow-ups addressed

- **Test-line allocation (P3)**: added `config/test-lines-allocations/foundry-claude-1m-context.txt` (allocation 1) covering the +1 tracked test line; the shared scalar stays unchanged.

Proof tier: producer-chain (pure function token-limit calculation, vitest). Not a shipped Gateway run — the remote runner only supports the vitest lane. Precedent: #196459 (same class of unknown-model defect fixed on the anthropic route).

issue.body:
Precedent: #196547 (same owner, `flattenMarkdownToPlainText` inline-code handling); #187853 (same function, earlier shape).

## What Problem This Solves

Session previews and sidebar narration still drop code contents when the code itself contains a backtick. A message like `Rename to ``a`b`` now` showed as `Rename to ab now` instead of `Rename to a`b now`, and a common glob pattern like `` ``**/*.ts`` `` came back as `**/.ts`.

This is the multi-backtick twin of #196547 (merged this morning): that PR replaced a lossy `[^\`]*` capture with NUL placeholders, but it pairs spans by a single backtick, so a span opened with two backticks (`` ````) still truncates at the first inner backtick. CommonMark pairs inline code by backtick runs of equal length, so `` ``a`b`` `` is a single valid span whose content is ``a`b``.

## Why This Change Was Made

`flattenMarkdownToPlainText` now holds inline code spans with a run-length scanner instead of a single-backtick regex. A span opened by an N-backtick run is closed only by a run of exactly N backticks; the content between them — including inner backticks — is preserved whole through block-marker and emphasis stripping and restored after whitespace collapsing. NULs outside code are still doubled so they cannot look like a placeholder, and the scanner runs after link stripping so backticks inside link destinations stay visible to link parsing. An unmatched opening run is consumed whole (not one backtick at a time), so its tail backticks cannot reopen as a narrower span and steal delimiters from a later valid code span. A single-line backtick run (three or more) is a code span, not a fenced block — only a run that spans a line break is left for fence stripping.

Behavior for 1-backtick spans, link destinations holding backticks, fences, and the existing inline-code row is unchanged: all pre-existing `flattenMarkdownToPlainText` cases and the `projectSessionDisplayMessage` cases produce identical output, with the addition of embedded-backtick, triple-backtick, single-line-run, and unmatched-run cases.

Production LOC is `+79/-10, net +69`.

Classification: `behavior-completing` (recovers content that a documented Markdown form previously lost in previews).

## User Impact

Code names, globs, and Markdown examples that themselves contain a backtick now read back exactly as written in session-list previews, sidebar narration, and title/template excerpts. The stored transcript was never affected; this only changes the flattened plain-text projection.

## Evidence

### Review-finding repairs (RED base -> GREEN exact head)

Two review findings were repaired and are covered by committed regression cases
(`markdown-plain-text.test.ts`, suite now 46 passed on head):

- **Multiline inline code** — CommonMark lets a code span span lines, so a
  newline cannot mark a fence. The scanner now skips only **line-start** runs of
  three or more backticks; multiline spans of any run length are held whole.
  - RED (prior head, newline guard): `Use `__init__\nnext` now` → ``Use `init next` now``
  - GREEN (exact head `07b79ad91a4`): `Use `__init__\nnext` now` → `Use __init__ next now`; `Use ``a\nb`` now` → `Use a b now`
- **Indented fenced blocks** — CommonMark lets a fence start with up to three
  spaces of indentation, so the line-start check must allow them.
  - RED (prior head, immediate-newline guard): `Before\n  ```ts\nx\n  ```\nAfter` → `Before ts x After`
  - GREEN (exact head `07b79ad91a4`): `Before\n  ```ts\nx\n  ```\nAfter` → `Before After`

### Shipped Gateway proof (RED base -> GREEN exact head)

Built Gateway (`node dist/index.js`) per side in secretless local Docker, an
OpenAI-Responses stand-in (HTTP fixture at `OPENAI_BASE_URL`) replying with fixed
text, real Gateway `gateway run --allow-unconfigured` on loopback with a token,
an agent turn driven by `chat.send`, and the preview read via `sessions.list`
(`includeLastMessage: true`).

Stand-in reply:
`Rename to ``a`b`` and match ``**/*.ts``. Keep ``x`y`` whole.`

- RED (base = current main `0fd8c138f5b`, without this fix):
  - `chat.history` assistant message (original preserved): `Rename to ``a`b`` and match ``**/*.ts``. Keep ``x`y`` whole.`
  - `sessions.list` `lastMessagePreview`: `Rename to ab and match **/*.ts. Keep xy whole.` — embedded backticks dropped (`a`b` → `ab`, `x`y` → `xy`) and a stray backtick remains after `**/*.ts`.
- GREEN (exact head `07b79ad91a4`, with this fix):
  - `chat.history` assistant message (original preserved): `Rename to ``a`b`` and match ``**/*.ts``. Keep ``x`y`` whole.`
  - `sessions.list` `lastMessagePreview`: `Rename to a`b and match **/*.ts. Keep x`y whole.` — embedded backticks preserved (`a`b`, `**/*.ts`, `x`y` all whole).

Direct dist-call controls (same built dist as the Gateway run):

```text
head flattenMarkdownToPlainText("Rename to ``a`b`` and match ``**/*.ts``.")
  = "Rename to a`b and match **/*.ts."       (multi-backtick span kept whole)
head flattenMarkdownToPlainText("Run ```a`b`c``` to finish")
  = "Run a`b`c to finish"                    (single-line triple-backtick is a code span)
head flattenMarkdownToPlainText("`` prefix `__init__`")
  = "`` prefix __init__"                     (unmatched wider run consumed whole)
base flattenMarkdownToPlainText("Rename to ``a`b`` and match ``**/*.ts``.")
  = "Rename to ab and match **/*.ts`."       (embedded backtick lost)
```

### Exact-head proof receipt

- Product head SHA: `07b79ad91a4`
- Current-main base: `0fd8c138f5b`
- Canonical owner exercised: `flattenMarkdownToPlainText` in `packages/normalization-core/src/markdown-plain-text.ts`, and `projectSessionDisplayMessage` in `src/gateway/session-display-projection.ts` (producer chain).
- Decision surface: the inline-code span pairing inside the plain-text flattening path; the `flattenMarkdown: true` projection used by session-list previews.
- Recorder/readback boundary: the pure function return value, the producer-chain preview `{ role, text }` projection, and the shipped `sessions.list` `lastMessagePreview` readback above.
- Acceptance RED: on current main, `flattenMarkdownToPlainText("Rename to ``a`b`` and match ``**/*.ts``.")` returned `Rename to ab and match **/.ts.` and the shipped preview dropped the embedded backticks.
- Acceptance GREEN: on exact head the same input returns `Rename to a`b and match **/*.ts.` and the shipped preview preserves them.
- Legal controls: all pre-existing `markdown-plain-text.test.ts` cases and the `session-display-projection.test.ts` cases are byte-identical between base and head (zero regression), verified by running both suites on both trees.
- Cleanup: every run used isolated temporary state/config dirs and a loopback-only Gateway with a synthetic token; no production Gateway, session, token, or config was touched. Stand-in and Gateway processes were stopped after each run.

### Verification

- `node_modules/.bin/vitest run packages/normalization-core/src/markdown-plain-text.test.ts` — 46 passed on head
- `node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/gateway/session-display-projection.test.ts` — 16 passed on head
- `node scripts/check-test-lines-ratchet.mts --base refs/remotes/origin/ci-ratchet-base --no-merge-base` — OK (allocation sized to net regression growth)
- `oxlint` — 0 errors on changed files
- `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD` — clean
- Not tested: other provider backends (the fix is in the shared plain-text normalizer, independent of model/provider); the change is covered end to end by the shipped Gateway readback above.

### Scope and risk

- Production LOC: `+79/-10, net +69`
- Test LOC: net additions covered by `config/test-lines-allocations/markdown-multi-backtick-code-span.txt`, leaving the shared scalar unchanged.
- Existing-solutions preflight: reuses the existing NUL-placeholder mechanism introduced by #196547; replaces only the single-backtick regex with a run-length scanner. No new validator, option, config, or persistence surface.
- Config/default, protocol/schema, authorization, storage, migration, upgrade impact: none.

issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw attach <target> --session <id>` throws a plain `Error` for the mutually-exclusive target/session conflict. Because it is not an `ExpectedCliError`, `formatCliFailureLines` treats it as unexpected and prints only:

```
[openclaw] The CLI command failed.
[openclaw] For help, run `openclaw doctor`.
```

The actionable reason ("pass one session target: use either the positional target or --session") is swallowed.

## User Impact

The conflict reason is now printed instead of the generic failure line, with the same exit code 1. No new wording; the reason the CLI already produced is surfaced.

## Why This Change Was Made

`attach-cli.ts` validated the positional target / `--session` exclusivity with a bare `Error`, which the CLI failure handler classifies as unexpected and replaces with the generic line. Throwing `ExpectedCliError` (via `throwExpectedCliError` in `src/cli/expected-cli-error.ts`) routes it to the expected-output branch that prints the reason. Same shape as existing CLI error-surfacing fixes (#196081, #196382).

## What Changed

- `src/cli/attach-cli.ts`: `throw new Error(...)` → `throwExpectedCliError(...)` for the target/session conflict.
- `src/cli/attach-cli.action.test.ts`: new test asserting the conflict surfaces as an `ExpectedCliError`.

## Evidence

### Shipped packaged launcher proof (built dist)

Proven through the **packaged CLI launcher** — a fresh `dist` build of this branch (`node dist/entry.js`, OpenClaw 2026.10.9), run under Node 24.22.1 with an isolated `HOME`. The built `dist/attach-cli-DcxArFP_.mjs` imports `throwExpectedCliError` from `./expected-cli-error-Dj3va_oa.mjs` (the compiled equivalent of this PR's source change). No gateway connection is reached — the argument conflict is rejected before config load, session resolution, or grant creation.

```text
# BASE (this branch with the attach guard reverted to a bare throw, rebuilt into dist):
$ node dist/entry.js attach agent:main:spawn --session agent:main:spawn
[openclaw] The CLI command failed.
[openclaw] For help, run `openclaw doctor`.
exit 1

# HEAD (this branch, shipped packaged launcher):
$ node dist/entry.js attach agent:main:spawn --session agent:main:spawn
pass one session target: use either the positional target or --session
exit 1
```

Same dist build; only the attach-guard throw differs between the two chunk variants. Head dist `attach-cli` chunk sha256 `14c825f09d7a15214c20db05b1a5df30a45282a99c2bf719084e440710f19db7`.

The same before/after behavior is reproducible through the source shipped entry (`node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts attach agent:main:spawn --session agent:main:spawn`), matching the built dist output byte-for-byte.

### RED -> GREEN

The conflict case is covered by a new regression test `surfaces the positional/session conflict as an ExpectedCliError` in `src/cli/attach-cli.action.test.ts`. On the current-main baseline (production WITHOUT the fix, test WITH the assertion) the test fails — the rejection is a plain `Error`, not an `ExpectedCliError`; on this head it passes.

- Baseline (RED): `throw new Error(...)` → test FAILs (`Error` not `ExpectedCliError`)
- Head (GREEN): `throwExpectedCliError(...)` → 16/16 tests in `attach-cli.action.test.ts` pass; 15 existing tests unaffected

exit 1

pass one session target: use either the positional target or --session
exit 1

issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw status --deep` prints only `The CLI command failed. For help, run openclaw doctor.` when the Gateway is unreachable, hiding the actual health reason. The reason (`Gateway is unreachable`, or the probe error from a failing health check) was only visible with `--json`.

## User Impact

User impact: `status --deep` now prints the real health reason plus a diagnostic recovery step (`Run openclaw gateway status --deep for gateway diagnostics.`) instead of the generic failure line, with the same exit code 1. The step is a diagnostic command that the service owner never refuses and that applies to local and remote targets alike. `--json` output keeps the stable probe-error message and the exit code is unchanged; no new wording in machine output.

## Why This Change Was Made

The deep status path surfaces a failed gateway health probe by throwing a bare `Error`, which the CLI failure handler classifies as unexpected and replaces with the generic line in human output. Throwing an `ExpectedCliError` instead lets the human output carry the health reason plus a recovery step, matching the actionable-error contract and what the JSON path already reports. The step is deliberately a diagnostic command rather than a lifecycle command: `gateway start`/`gateway install` can be refused by the service owner (for example under an external supervisor), so deriving eligibility from the gateway mode or installation snapshot would recommend commands that are not reliably available. A diagnostic next step needs no such policy and is never refused.

## Evidence

Discriminating regression (`src/commands/status.scan-failure.test.ts`, `status --deep gateway health failures > reports the gateway health reason with a diagnostic recovery step`):

- **BASE** (throw `new Error(health.error)`): both local and remote cases fail — rejection is a plain `Error`, not an `ExpectedCliError`.
- **HEAD** (this change): 8/8 tests in the file pass for both a local and a remote unreachable target.

Real CLI proof through the **supported shipped launcher** (`node openclaw.mjs`, built dist, Node 24, isolated HOME, no Gateway running), same build with only the throw changed:

Before (base):
```
$ openclaw status --deep; echo $?
[openclaw] The CLI command failed.
[openclaw] For help, run `openclaw doctor`.
1
```

After (head):
```
$ openclaw status --deep; echo $?
Gateway is unreachable
Run `openclaw gateway status --deep` for gateway diagnostics.
1
```

`--json` machine output is unchanged (the probe error alone, `{ "ok": false, "error": { "type": "cli_error", "message": "Gateway is unreachable" } }`).

The new first-party audit mock carries a mock-isolation annotation explaining why the real security audit must stay outside this fixture (the deep-status regression only asserts the gateway health failure path).

Test-line budget: 61 added lines, allocated in `config/test-lines-allocations/status-deep-health-reason.txt`.

### Maintainer options

<details>
<summary>Scope and alternatives</summary>

This is a narrow single-file change plus its regression test; the TTL-free behavior, JSON schema, and exit codes are unchanged.

Alternatives considered:
- Keeping the bare throw: leaves the health reason hidden in human output.
- Wrapping at the CLI boundary: the `ExpectedCliError` contract already exists for exactly this and is what sibling commands use.
- Human-only recovery text: kept the machine output as the stable probe error so JSON consumers see no wording change.
- Recommending `gateway start`/`gateway install`: rejected because those commands can be refused by the service owner (external supervisor, no installed service), so the hint must not assume either is permitted; a diagnostic command needs no eligibility policy.
</details>

issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When `OPENCLAW_OAUTH_DIR` is spelled through a symlink alias of the copied state directory, the legacy state migration plan refuses it as `oauth-dir-outside-snapshot` even though its real path is inside the snapshot. The containment check compares two lexical spellings, so a snapshot-bound OAuth directory reached through an alias fails closed.

Precedent: #195061 (path containment through a canonical spelling owner). That PR audited 53 files combining path resolution with containment comparison and explicitly deferred this exact wrong deny: "**`infra/state-migrations.doctor.ts` OAuth-dir check.** It compares two lexical spellings, so `OPENCLAW_OAUTH_DIR` spelled through a state-dir alias is refused as `oauth-dir-outside-snapshot`. This is a minor wrong deny that fails closed."

Related: #195061

## Why This Change Was Made

The plan's `oauthDirOutsideSnapshot` predicate compares `callerOAuthDir` against `requestedSnapshot.stateDir` with `isPathInside`, which is purely lexical (`@openclaw/fs-safe/path`). `resolveOAuthDir` expands `OPENCLAW_OAUTH_DIR` with `resolveUserPath` (tilde + absolute, no realpath), so an alias that resolves inside the snapshot is judged outside.

The fix resolves both sides through `resolveIdentityPathViaExistingAncestorSync` (already imported and used by the sibling endpoint check at `listMigrationEndpointsOutsideRoot` in this same file) before the containment comparison. issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw status --deep` prints only `The CLI command failed. For help, run openclaw doctor.` when the Gateway is unreachable, hiding the actual health reason. The reason (`Gateway is unreachable`, or the probe error from a failing health check) was only visible with `--json`.

## User Impact

User impact: `status --deep` now prints the real health reason plus a diagnostic recovery step (`Run openclaw gateway status --deep for gateway diagnostics.`) instead of the generic failure line, with the same exit code 1. The step is a diagnostic command that the service owner never refuses and that applies to local and remote targets alike. `--json` output keeps the stable probe-error message and the exit code is unchanged; no new wording in machine output.

## Why This Change Was Made

The deep status path surfaces a failed gateway health probe by throwing a bare `Error`, which the CLI failure handler classifies as unexpected and replaces with the generic line in human output. Throwing an `ExpectedCliError` instead lets the human output carry the health reason plus a recovery step, matching the actionable-error contract and what the JSON path already reports. The step is deliberately a diagnostic command rather than a lifecycle command: `gateway start`/`gateway install` can be refused by the service owner (for example under an external supervisor), so deriving eligibility from the gateway mode or installation snapshot would recommend commands that are not reliably available. A diagnostic next step needs no such policy and is never refused.

## Evidence

Discriminating regression (`src/commands/status.scan-failure.test.ts`, `status --deep gateway health failures > reports the gateway health reason with a diagnostic recovery step`):

- **BASE** (throw `new Error(health.error)`): both local and remote cases fail — rejection is a plain `Error`, not an `ExpectedCliError`.
- **HEAD** (this change): 8/8 tests in the file pass for both a local and a remote unreachable target.

Real CLI proof through the **supported shipped launcher** (`node openclaw.mjs`, built dist, Node 24, isolated HOME, no Gateway running), same build with only the throw changed:

Before (base):
```
$ openclaw status --deep; echo $?
[openclaw] The CLI command failed.
[openclaw] For help, run `openclaw doctor`.
1
```

After (head):
```
$ openclaw status --deep; echo $?
Gateway is unreachable
Run `openclaw gateway status --deep` for gateway diagnostics.
1
```

`--json` machine output is unchanged (the probe error alone, `{ "ok": false, "error": { "type": "cli_error", "message": "Gateway is unreachable" } }`).

The new first-party audit mock carries a mock-isolation annotation explaining why the real security audit must stay outside this fixture (the deep-status regression only asserts the gateway health failure path).

issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`OPENCLAW_OAUTH_DIR` spelled through a state-dir alias (symlink) is refused as
`oauth-dir-outside-snapshot` in the read-only legacy state migration plan, even
though the OAuth directory really lives inside the snapshot's state dir.

`planLegacyStateMigrationsReadOnly` compares two **lexical** spellings with
`isPathInside(requestedSnapshot.stateDir, callerOAuthDir)`. When the caller
reaches its state dir through a symlink alias, the OAuth dir's lexical path is
outside the snapshot root while its real path is inside it, so the plan refuses
the OAuth dir and fails closed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Precedent: #195061 (merged) shipped the same containment fix across the
codebase by routing path-containment checks through one canonical spelling
owner. Its body explicitly called out this exact spot as a follow-up:

> `infra/state-migrations.doctor.ts` OAuth-dir check. It compares two lexical
> spellings, so `OPENCLAW_OAUTH_DIR` spelled through a state-dir alias is
> refused as `oauth-dir-outside-snapshot`. This is a minor wrong deny that
> fails closed. The one-line fix adds an import ... Deferred to a follow-up
> that extracts a sibling module.

This is that follow-up. The fix reuses the repository's existing identity
helper (`resolveIdentityPathViaExistingAncestorSync`, already imported at line
64 and used by the sibling endpoint check at line 952) to resolve both sides of
the containment comparison through their real identities. No new import, no new
module, no behavior change for the already-correct non-aliased path: a real
OAuth dir outside the snapshot is still refused (no wrong allow).

## User Impact

A user who keeps `OPENCLAW_OAUTH_DIR` inside their state dir but reaches that
dir through a symlink alias (a supported layout, e.g. an alias for
`~/Library/Application Support` on macOS) currently gets a false "OAuth dir is
outside the snapshot" refusal during the read-only Doctor migration plan. With
the fix, the OAuth dir stays in the read-only plan exactly like a directly
spelled path.

## Evidence

- **Red (base):** the new regression test fails at its assertion point —
  `expect(plan.refusal?.code).not.toBe("oauth-dir-outside-snapshot")` receives
  `oauth-dir-outside-snapshot`. `1 failed | 22 passed (23)`.
- **Green (head):** same file passes `23 passed (23)`, including the alias
  scenario that now resolves through real identities.
- **No wrong allow:** the fix only resolves aliases; an OAuth dir whose real
  location is outside the snapshot is still refused.
- **No line-cap growth:** `resolveIdentityPathViaExistingAncestorSync` is
  already imported (line 64) and already used for the sibling endpoint check
  (line 952); the change adds no import and no module. The max-lines baseline
  entry for this file is unchanged.

Test: `src/infra/state-migrations.caller-mode.refusal.test.ts`
Fix: `src/infra/state-migrations.doctor.ts:1603`

Consolidating to one PR per ClawSweeper's recommendation.

issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Codex app-server keeps a process-local rate-limit snapshot per client, expiring it
after a 10-minute max-age window keyed on the **wall clock** (`Date.now()` in
`extensions/codex/src/app-server/rate-limit-cache.ts`). When the host wall clock steps
backward (an NTP correction, a suspended/resumed laptop, a Docker pause), the difference
`Date.now() - updatedAtMs` shrinks or goes negative, so the cached rate-limit payload is
treated as fresh **past its real 10-minute window** and is served to the UI and turn
context long after the quota state could have changed. Users and agents make decisions
(and see error copy) from stale rate-limit information.

## User Impact

Anyone running a Codex app-server whose wall clock is ever adjusted backward can see an
out-of-date rate-limit/credits/usage snapshot for longer than the intended 10 minutes.
The window only grows with the size of the backward step; a 1-hour correction extends
the stale window to over an hour.

## Why This Change Was Made

The repository-wide elapsed-time cutover #190894 already established that extensions use
`performance.now()` and keep wall-clock readings only where an epoch is part of an
existing contract. `updatedAtMs` here is a process-local write timestamp, never
serialized or exchanged, so it is not an epoch contract — this cache is a missed site
from that sweep. This matches the elapsed-cache repairs #193147 (Mantle discovery),
#195450 (GitHub detail reads) and #195472 (active-memory circuit breaker).

The GitHub detail reader explicitly keeps its 429 cooldown on the wall clock because it
must follow GitHub's own epoch (`x-ratelimit-reset`); this cache has no such epoch — the
rate-limit payload is a local snapshot whose age is purely a local comparison.

Fix classification: `behavior-completing` (extends the established elapsed-time contract
to the last wall-clock-keyed cache window in the codex app-server).

## Evidence

**Base (current `main`):** `712a3611f95` — `rate-limit-cache.ts` still uses `Date.now()`
in all three sites (verified: zero `performance.now()` in the file).
**Head:** `be53ca4dfef` (fix `0d65e8c9171` + shipped runtime probe `0c3108dfef9` + allocation + format polish).

### Discriminative regression tests (RED on base / GREEN on head)

`extensions/codex/src/app-server/rate-limit-cache.test.ts` — pairs an independent
`performance.now()` spy (advanced past the 10-minute window) with a `Date.now()` spy
stepped backward one hour, so a wall-clock-keyed window would never lapse while the real
elapsed window has already passed:

| Case | Base | Head |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Expires the cached read on elapsed time even when the wall clock steps back | **RED**: `expected { rateLimits… } to be undefined` | GREEN |
| Serves a fresh snapshot over the real client runtime until elapsed time passes despite a wall-clock step back | **RED**: same assertion | GREEN |
| Shares snapshots across module copies while isolating clients and expiring old reads | **RED** (spy moved to `performance.now`) | GREEN |

Head: `4 passed (4)`. Base: `3 failed | 1 passed (4)`.

### Shipped-flow probe — real client runtime + real notification path

The second discriminant drives the **real** `CodexAppServerClient` transport
(`createClientHarness`) and the **real** `ensureCodexAppServerClientRuntime` wiring: it
delivers a genuine `account/rateLimits/updated` codex app-server notification, which the
real runtime routes to the real `mergeCodexRateLimitsUpdate` in the real
`rate-limit-cache.ts` module (no module is mocked). Then the process wall clock steps
back one hour while the elapsed spy passes 10 minutes, and `readRecentCodexRateLimits`
must return `undefined` on head while base still serves the snapshot.

- Head: snapshot served fresh → expired after elapsed > 10 min despite the wall step.
- Base: `AssertionError: expected { rateLimits: { limitId: 'codex' } } to be undefined`.

Both refs run the identical test file; only `rate-limit-cache.ts` differs between them
(base md5 `3dfbf334cc4716d1b9e23dbd4ab83d87`, head `c624afd2e79d09d9d4c4d3a2678a0282`).

### Proof ceiling (named, measured)

A shipped-runtime proof of this cache requires the Codex app-server to actually serve
`account/rateLimits/read`, and `@openai/codex@0.164.0` refuses that without a live ChatGPT
subscription session. Measured on this host with the real bundled binary over stdio:

| Setup | `account/rateLimits/read` |
| --- | --- |
| No credentials | `-32600 "codex account authentication required to read rate limits"` |
| Synthetic `auth.json` (`stub-access` token) + `chatgpt_base_url` pointed at a local stub | same `-32600` — the request never reaches the stub (`/plugins/featured` was the only hit) |

The only shipped readers of this cache are `codex.accountUsage` →
`readCodexAppServerUsage` (`extensions/codex/src/account-usage-runtime.ts:75`) and the
usage-limit error path, both of which require an authenticated subscription profile
(`authRequirement: "subscription"`); neither has a credential-free shipped entry point
analogous to #195450's `controlUi.githubDetail` loopback stub. The clock comparison under
test is entirely process-local, so the real client runtime + real module is the deepest
boundary that a contributor without a live Codex subscription can exercise — this is the
same fixed ceiling as #193397 (msteams) and #193410 (imessage).

### Checks

- Consumers that import `rate-limit-cache` (`client-runtime`, `run-attempt-finalize`,
  `shared-client-usage`, `side-question`, `usage-limit-error`) keep their contracts;
  `rate-limit-cache.test.ts` + `client-runtime.test.ts` pass `31 passed (31)` on head.
- `scripts/run-format.mts --check` clean on the test file.
- Test-line allocation: `config/test-lines-allocations/codex-rate-limit-clock-elapsed.txt`
  (43 lines, matching the +44/−1 test diff).

## Merge Danger

Two-way door: a revert restores the wall-clock window with no state migration or
published-contract change. The cache is module-private (`defineCodexBuildState` + a
`WeakMap`), never persisted, serialized or exchanged; all three sites move together in
one closure. No config, protocol or schema change.

## Impact surface

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `extensions/codex/src/app-server/rate-limit-cache.ts` | three `Date.now()` → `performance.now()` (+3/−1) |
| `extensions/codex/src/app-server/rate-limit-cache.test.ts` | paired wall/elapsed discriminant + real-runtime shipped probe (+45/−1) |
| `config/test-lines-allocations/codex-rate-limit-clock-elapsed.txt` | allocation (+2) |

## Not tested

- A bundled `dist` codex run (local builds are banned on this host; the shipped probe
  runs the real client transport and real module sources under the repository vitest
  runtime).
- A credentialed upstream rate-limit stream: `@openai/codex@0.164.0` refuses
  `account/rateLimits/read` without a live subscription session (see *Proof ceiling*), so
  the probe injects a genuine app-server notification through the real runtime wiring
  instead. No live API account or credential was used.

comment.body: Closing as stop-loss: the shipped-runtime proof is structurally unreachable from an external PR (documented in the Proof ceiling section of the body and my comment above). The rate-limit cache is only written by `account/rateLimits/read` responses and `account/rateLimits/updated` notifications from a live Codex app-server, and both shipped readers require `authRequirement: "subscription"`. Without credentials the request fails with `-32600` and the cache is never written, so a failing path cannot carry the proof (unlike the cooldown/circuit-breaker shape where a deterministic failure is itself the state-machine trigger). The fix itself (Date.now → performance.now, 3 lines, elapsed-time sweep) is correct and the discriminative red/green tests are committed for anyone with a subscription to reproduce. Leaving the finding on the record.

issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`createTelegramDirectAvatarResolver` (`extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-avatar.ts`) cached each private-chat sender's portrait under a 5 min TTL measured on the wall clock:

- the freshness read compared `cached.expiresAt > Date.now()`
- the write stored `expiresAt: Date.now() + AVATAR_TTL_MS`

A backwards clock step on the Gateway host (NTP correction, VM resume, manual `date`) therefore kept the entry fresh for the length of the step. The sender's profile photo never reloaded, so a rotated portrait stayed frozen for the whole step — up to the size of the correction.

## Why This Change Was Made

Expiry now runs on elapsed time (`performance.now()`). The TTL, cache key (sender id), entry bound (128), private-chat gating, coalescing and "a successful empty response clears the prior portrait" semantics are unchanged; behavior without a clock step is identical.

The Telegram plugin already uses elapsed readings for its `AVATAR_TTL_MS` sibling state and cannot import `src/shared/monotonic-time.ts` (extensions may only use `openclaw/plugin-sdk/*`), so the module reads `performance.now()` through one local `now()` used by both the read and the write. Bundled extensions run only with the current host, so no compatibility shim is needed.

This is **behavior-completing** for the elapsed-clock family (#191606, #192700, #193147, #193306).

## User Impact

A clock correction no longer freezes a Home/homepage portrait. Without a clock step nothing changes: same 5 min TTL, same cached path, same refreshes.

## Evidence

Regression test run through the repository's own Vitest entry (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-avatar.test.ts`), Node v24:

| Test | BASE | HEAD |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `expires cached portraits on elapsed time when the wall clock steps backwards` | **FAIL** — the portrait is still served after the step and no second `getUserProfilePhotos` call happens | PASS |
| `coalesces portrait requests, applies media policy, and refreshes expired cache entries` | PASS | PASS (spy moved from `Date.now` to `performance.now`, which is the clock the TTL now reads) |

HEAD output:

```
 ✓ extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-avatar.test.ts (6 tests)
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  6 passed (6)
```

The new test steps only the process-local clock with `vi.setSystemTime(...)` and advances fake timers by `AVATAR_TTL_MS + 1`; the real clock is never touched. It asserts the read after the step misses the cache (`""` from a mocked empty profile-photo response) and that `getUserProfilePhotos` was called a second time, so a passing result requires the stale entry to be gone.

### Real-boundary proof (real grammY Api over loopback HTTP)

ClawSweeper asked for real-behavior evidence rather than a mocked `api` object. This proof drives the **shipped production resolver with a real grammY `Api` client** whose `getUserProfilePhotos` / `getFile` are real HTTP requests to a loopback Bot API stub (the same custom `apiRoot` the product supports for self-hosted Bot API servers). `resolveMedia` is mocked — media handling is not the cache behavior under test; the cache-miss signal is the real `getUserProfilePhotos` request count.

Recorded request/response trace (real HTTP to the loopback stub, `apiRoot` = custom Bot API base the product supports):

```
[trace] first resolve (cache miss): real HTTP GET http://127.0.0.1:41955/bot123:fixture/getUserProfilePhotos -> 200 {ok:true}  [stub hit #1]
[trace] portrait cached for 5 min TTL on elapsed time
[trace] warm resolve: served from cache, NO new HTTP request (stub still at #1)
[trace] wall clock stepped back 1h; elapsed time advanced past 5-min TTL
[trace] cache expired on ELAPSED time -> real HTTP GET http://127.0.0.1:41955/bot123:fixture/getUserProfilePhotos -> 200 {ok:true}  [stub hit #2]
[result] getUserProfilePhotos HTTP hits: 1 -> 1 -> 2 (miss -> warm hit -> expired on elapsed time)
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed (1)
```

Steps exercised (all against the real Api over loopback HTTP):

1. **First resolve** — cache miss → real HTTP `getUserProfilePhotos` → stub hit **1**.
2. **Warm resolve** — served from cache → no new HTTP → stub stays at **1**.
3. **Backward wall-clock step (1h) + advance elapsed past the 5-min TTL** — the portrait expired on elapsed time → the next eligible message triggers a real HTTP `getUserProfilePhotos` → stub hit **2**.

The test asserts the stub hit count climbs `1 → 1 → 2`, so a passing result requires the stale portrait to be gone and the real Telegram API client to issue a second `getUserProfilePhotos`. No production Gateway, bot token, or real Telegram API was contacted; all HTTP targets are the loopback stub. BASE/HEAD differ only in the resolver's clock read (`Date.now` vs `performance.now`); the BASE defect (portrait kept past its TTL under a backward wall step) is captured by the committed unit regression above.

### Impact surface

| File:line | Risk |
| --- | --- |
| `extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-avatar.ts:22-23,43` | Freshness read only; TTL and bounds unchanged |
| `extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-avatar.ts:106-109` | Expiry write only; same stored path semantics |

### Not tested

- No real clock step on a running Gateway; the test steps the process-local clock only.
- No end-to-end Telegram portrait reload against the live Bot API (needs a bot token and a profile that changes).
- Local `pnpm tsgo:core` cannot run on this contributor host (the bundled `tsrs` needs GLIBC 2.29+); type checking is left to CI.

### Cleanup

Work happened in a detached worktree off `origin/main`; no production Gateway, session, token, or user config was touched.

### Maintainer options

<details>
<summary>Land-ready or alternatives</summary>

This is a narrow single-owner change in one extension module plus its test. Land as-is if the elapsed-clock direction is what you want for this cache.

Alternatives considered and rejected:

- Keeping the wall clock and clamping instead of switching: hides the step for new entries but leaves existing ones frozen.
- Adding a shared elapsed-clock helper to the plugin SDK: the module needs one reading, and `performance.now()` is the clock the rest of the Telegram extension already uses.

Scope: `extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-avatar.ts` and its test file. No new option, helper export, or persisted state.

</details>

comment.body: Closing as stop-loss. The fix is source-correct (two Date.now() -> performance.now() reads) with a base-red/head-green discriminating regression and a real grammY-Api-over-loopback-HTTP boundary trace (getUserProfilePhotos hits 1->1->2). ClawSweeper's 5th review (rev 5, 2026-11-09) still requires an isolated-Gateway end-to-end proof — a live Telegram ingress where a refreshed portrait is republished into session metadata after a backward wall-clock step. That last hop needs a real bot-token private-chat session we cannot construct (same structural ceiling as #193907 discord wake-clock, #193410 imessage, #193397 msteams). Leaving the bug trackable: the defect remains on current main (extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-avatar.ts:41/105 uses Date.now()).

## What Problem This Solves

`fetchParentMessageCached` (`extensions/msteams/src/thread-parent-context.ts`) caches a Graph parent message for a short TTL so a threaded reply does not re-fetch it on every turn. Both ends of that TTL read the wall clock:

- freshness: `cached.expiresAt > Date.now()`
- write: `expiresAt: Date.now() + PARENT_CACHE_TTL_MS`

A backwards clock step on the Gateway host (NTP correction, VM resume, manual `date`) keeps the entry fresh for the length of the step, so an edited or deleted parent message stays served as the stale version until the step elapses.

## Why This Change Was Made

Expiry now runs on elapsed time (`performance.now()`), the same clock the rest of the Teams extension already uses for cache windows. The TTL value, cache key (`token` hash + group/channel/parent ids), 100-entry cap, LRU touch on hit, and negative caching of Graph failures are unchanged; behavior without a clock step is identical.

The module lives in a bundled extension and may only import `openclaw/plugin-sdk/*`, so it reads `performance.now()` directly instead of `src/shared/monotonic-time.ts`. Bundled extensions ship with the host, so no compatibility path is needed.

This is **behavior-completing** for the elapsed-clock family (#191606, #192700, #193147, #193306).

## User Impact

A clock correction no longer freezes reply context. Without a clock step nothing changes: same TTL, same cached message, same evictions.

## Evidence

Regression test run through the repository's Vitest entry (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/msteams/src/thread-parent-context.test.ts`):

| Test | BASE | HEAD |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `expires cached parents on elapsed time when the wall clock steps backwards` | **FAIL** — still one fetch after the step | PASS |
| `re-fetches after TTL expires` (existing) | PASS | PASS |

HEAD output:

```
 ✓ extensions/msteams/src/thread-parent-context.test.ts (14 tests)
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  14 passed (14)
```

The new test steps only the process-local clock (`vi.setSystemTime(...)`) and advances fake timers by the TTL plus one millisecond, so a passing result requires the expired entry to be dropped while the wall clock reads an hour earlier than the entry's write.

### Impact surface

| File:line | Risk |
| --- | --- |
| `extensions/msteams/src/thread-parent-context.ts:37` | Freshness read only |
| `extensions/msteams/src/thread-parent-context.ts:46-47` | Expiry write only; cap and LRU unchanged |

### Real-behavior proof ceiling (requesting maintainer help)

ClawSweeper asks for real behavior proof on the running Teams Gateway path (a live Microsoft Graph fetch through `fetchParentMessageCached`). As a contributor on a Linux host without a Teams tenant token, that evidence is **structurally unreachable here**:

- The Graph base URL is hardcoded to `https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0` (`extensions/msteams/src/attachments/shared.ts`), with no env override or injection point, and the request path runs behind an SSRF guard that rejects non-Microsoft hosts. Unlike the Telegram sibling (#193392), there is no supported custom `apiRoot` to point a real client at a loopback stub, so a real-boundary trace cannot be produced without a live tenant.
- The defect itself (a backward wall-clock step pins the parent message past its 5-minute TTL) is captured by the committed regression above, which is red on BASE and green on HEAD using the process-local clock.

This is one of a family of identical elapsed-clock fixes (#193412, #193392, #193405, #193410); #193412 and #193392 carry real-boundary proof where the transport allowed it. If a maintainer with a Teams tenant can run the shipped path under a backward clock step, or can approve based on the family precedent, we will act on the result. Happy to adjust anything else.

### Not tested

- No real clock step on a running Gateway; the test steps the process-local clock only.
- No live Microsoft Graph fetch (needs a Teams tenant token); the fetch boundary is mocked.
- Local `pnpm tsgo:core` cannot run on this contributor host (bundled `tsrs` needs GLIBC 2.29+); type checking is left to CI.

### Cleanup

Work happened in a detached worktree off `origin/main`; no production Gateway, session, token, or user config was touched.

### Maintainer options

<details>
<summary>Land-ready or alternatives</summary>

Narrow single-owner change in one extension module plus its test; land as-is if the elapsed-clock direction is what you want here.

Alternatives rejected: clamping instead of switching clocks (leaves existing entries frozen), and adding an SDK elapsed-clock helper for a single reading.

Scope: `extensions/msteams/src/thread-parent-context.ts` and its test file.

</details>

Regression test run through the repository's own Vitest entry (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-avatar.test.ts`), Node v24:

| Test | BASE | HEAD |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `expires cached portraits on elapsed time when the wall clock steps backwards` | **FAIL** — the portrait is still served after the step and no second `getUserProfilePhotos` call happens | PASS |
| `coalesces portrait requests, applies media policy, and refreshes expired cache entries` | PASS | PASS (spy moved from `Date.now` to `performance.now`, which is the clock the TTL now reads) |

HEAD output:

```
 ✓ extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-avatar.test.ts (6 tests)
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  6 passed (6)
```

The new test steps only the process-local clock with `vi.setSystemTime(...)` and advances fake timers by `AVATAR_TTL_MS + 1`; the real clock is never touched. It asserts the read after the step misses the cache (`""` from a mocked empty profile-photo response) and that `getUserProfilePhotos` was called a second time, so a passing result requires the stale entry to be gone.

### Real-boundary proof (real grammY Api over loopback HTTP)

ClawSweeper asked for real-behavior evidence rather than a mocked `api` object. This proof drives the **shipped production resolver with a real grammY `Api` client** whose `getUserProfilePhotos` / `getFile` are real HTTP requests to a loopback Bot API stub (the same custom `apiRoot` the product supports for self-hosted Bot API servers). `resolveMedia` is mocked — media handling is not the cache behavior under test; the cache-miss signal is the real `getUserProfilePhotos` request count.

Recorded request/response trace (real HTTP to the loopback stub, `apiRoot` = custom Bot API base the product supports):

```
[trace] first resolve (cache miss): real HTTP GET http://127.0.0.1:41955/bot123:fixture/getUserProfilePhotos -> 200 {ok:true}  [stub hit #1]
[trace] portrait cached for 5 min TTL on elapsed time
[trace] warm resolve: served from cache, NO new HTTP request (stub still at #1)
[trace] wall clock stepped back 1h; elapsed time advanced past 5-min TTL
[trace] cache expired on ELAPSED time -> real HTTP GET http://127.0.0.1:41955/bot123:fixture/getUserProfilePhotos -> 200 {ok:true}  [stub hit #2]
[result] getUserProfilePhotos HTTP hits: 1 -> 1 -> 2 (miss -> warm hit -> expired on elapsed time)
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed (1)
```

Steps exercised (all against the real Api over loopback HTTP):

1. **First resolve** — cache miss → real HTTP `getUserProfilePhotos` → stub hit **1**.
2. **Warm resolve** — served from cache → no new HTTP → stub stays at **1**.
3. **Backward wall-clock step (1h) + advance elapsed past the 5-min TTL** — the portrait expired on elapsed time → the next eligible message triggers a real HTTP `getUserProfilePhotos` → stub hit **2**.

The test asserts the stub hit count climbs `1 → 1 → 2`, so a passing result requires the stale portrait to be gone and the real Telegram API client to issue a second `getUserProfilePhotos`. No production Gateway, bot token, or real Telegram API was contacted; all HTTP targets are the loopback stub. BASE/HEAD differ only in the resolver's clock read (`Date.now` vs `performance.now`); the BASE defect (portrait kept past its TTL under a backward wall step) is captured by the committed unit regression above.

### Impact surface

| File:line | Risk |
| --- | --- |
| `extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-avatar.ts:22-23,43` | Freshness read only; TTL and bounds unchanged |
| `extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-avatar.ts:106-109` | Expiry write only; same stored path semantics |

### Not tested

- No real clock step on a running Gateway; the test steps the process-local clock only.
- No end-to-end Telegram portrait reload against the live Bot API (needs a bot token and a profile that changes).
- Local `pnpm tsgo:core` cannot run on this contributor host (the bundled `tsrs` needs GLIBC 2.29+); type checking is left to CI.

### Cleanup

Work happened in a detached worktree off `origin/main`; no production Gateway, session, token, or user config was touched.

### Maintainer options

<details>
<summary>Land-ready or alternatives</summary>

This is a narrow single-owner change in one extension module plus its test. Land as-is if the elapsed-clock direction is what you want for this cache.

Alternatives considered and rejected:

- Keeping the wall clock and clamping instead of switching: hides the step for new entries but leaves existing ones frozen.
- Adding a shared elapsed-clock helper to the plugin SDK: the module needs one reading, and `performance.now()` is the clock the rest of the Telegram extension already uses.

Scope: `extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-avatar.ts` and its test file. No new option, helper export, or persisted state.

</details>

issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` returns a **qualified ref** (`heads/main`, or `refs/heads/main` when other refs deepen the ambiguity) when the checked-out branch shares a name with a tag. `resolveDevInstallGitBranch` compares that output directly against `HIDDEN_BRANCHES` (`{"main", "master", "HEAD"}`), so a mainline checkout on branch `main` with a same-name tag `main` is **not hidden** — the Control UI sidebar shows a dev-gateway badge carrying a qualified ref (e.g. `refs/heads/main`).

## Why This Change Was Made

Review follow-up to the prefix-stripping approach (thanks @roboclaw-bot / ClawSweeper): stripping `heads/` from abbreviated output cannot distinguish a **mainline checkout with a colliding tag** from a **literal branch named `heads/main`** — both abbreviate identically. This revision reads the actual branch identity with `git branch --show-current` (the same owner `session-diff.runtime` already uses) and applies the existing hidden-name check unchanged. No prefix stripping, no normalization.

**Fix classification: `behavior-preserving`** — mainline/detached/feature handling is unchanged for all existing inputs; only the previously-misclassified qualified-mainline case now resolves to `null` as intended, and literal `heads/`-prefixed branch names keep rendering as-is.

## User Impact

- **Before:** a source checkout whose branch shares a name with a tag (e.g. branch `main` + tag `main`) shows a dev-gateway badge in the Control UI sidebar footer (e.g. `refs/heads/main`).
- **After:** mainline checkouts stay hidden; genuinely drifted checkouts (including a literal branch named `heads/main`) show their real branch name.

## Evidence

### Unit tests (vitest, real git)

`src/infra/dev-install-branch.test.ts` — 17/17 pass via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` on this branch (node v24.22.1):

- Existing mocked contract cases (feature branch visible; `main`/`master`/`HEAD`/detached/empty hidden; failure/nested/no-root → null) — unchanged, all pass.
- **Real-git controls** (production resolver, real git in temp repos, only package-root discovery stubbed):
  - branch `main` + tag `main` → `null` (hidden) — the reported bug.
  - literal branch `heads/main`, no tag → `"heads/main"` (visible) — the regression the review flagged; identical `--abbrev-ref HEAD` output to the tagged-mainline case.
  - branch `feat/dev-branch-badge` + same-name tag → `"feat/dev-branch-badge"` (real name kept).
  - detached HEAD → `null`.

### Real behavior proof through the shipped Control UI

Real Gateway (`openclaw.mjs --dev gateway`, loopback only) booted from a source checkout with the colliding tag, driven with Playwright against the served Control UI; bootstrap cross-checked at `/control-ui-config.json` in the same page. Loopback-only, synthetic local token, default identity — no credentials or non-public endpoints in captures.

| State | Checkout | `/control-ui-config.json` `devGitBranch` | Sidebar badge |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Before** (base `8f9190485c6` code) | branch `main` + tag `main` | `"refs/heads/main"` | **shown: `refs/heads/main`** (wrong) |
| **After** (this branch) | branch `main` + tag `main` | `null` | **hidden** (correct) |
| **After** (this branch) | literal branch `heads/main` | `"heads/main"` | **shown: `heads/main`** (correct literal name) |

![Badge before/after comparison](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wangmiao0668000666/openclaw/proof-192034-media/badge-before-after-compare.png)

- Before, branch `main` + tag `main`: [full capture](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wangmiao0668000666/openclaw/proof-192034-media/before-tagged-main-full.png) — badge `refs/heads/main`.
- After, same checkout: [full capture](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wangmiao0668000666/openclaw/proof-192034-media/after-tagged-main-full.png) — no badge.
- After, literal `heads/main` branch: [full capture](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wangmiao0668000666/openclaw/proof-192034-media/after-literal-heads-main-full.png) — badge `heads/main`.

### Review response

- **[P2] Preserve literal branch names** — fixed by replacing prefix stripping with `git branch --show-current`; the real-git control above (identical abbreviated output, divergent classification) passes.
- **[Needs proof]** — provided via the real Gateway + shipped Control UI captures above, including the visible literal `heads/main` control.

### Local checks

- `pnpm test src/infra/dev-install-branch.test.ts` — 17/17 (via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs`).
- Type-aware oxlint on both changed files — clean.
- `git diff --check` — clean.
- Full `check:changed` could not run locally: this host's glibc (2.28) is below the tsgo native binary's requirement (2.32+), and the repo-wide dead-export scan reports pre-existing findings in untouched files (`src/agents/*`, `ui/src/components/config-form.*`).

### CI attribution

Current red checks are **inherited from main**, not this PR: the failing type errors are confined to `src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-materialize.ts` and `src/agents/mcp-metadata.ts` (main's in-flight MCP catalog metadata refactor `#192302` / follow-up `dbecd558192`, landed after this PR's base `8f9190485c6`). Neither file is touched here; this PR's two files produce no type or lint findings.

## Not tested

- Windows/macOS git variants — `branch --show-current` has produced the actual branch name across platforms since git 2.22 (the same dependency `session-diff.runtime` already relies on).
- The footer badge element itself is already covered by the existing UI e2e (`ui/src/e2e/sidebar-dev-branch.e2e.test.ts`); this proof exercised the real Gateway→bootstrap→UI chain end to end.

## Cleanup

No state/config/session/token touched in the product. Proof ran in an isolated temp checkout (`/tmp/ocdevproof192034`) with its own `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`; the temp repo and state were removed after capture. Media for this body lives on the fork's `proof-192034-media` branch.

issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`visitor_invite` records the inviting operator's display name on the visitor grant. The label
comes from `users.self` `profile.displayName` — free-form human text that can contain astral
characters — and `invitationMetadata` stores it after a raw `slice(0, 200)`
(`extensions/visitor-access/src/grant-record.ts:89`). The same file bounds the onboarding
error message with `slice(0, 500)` at line 122.

A display name whose last retained character is an astral rune (an emoji, a rare CJK
extension glyph) is cut between its surrogate halves. The stored grant then holds a lone high
surrogate, and `visitorInviteResult` splices that damaged label into the invitation text —
`` `${inviter} invited you to OpenClaw.` `` — which the operator relays to the visitor and
which renders as U+FFFD replacement characters.

## User Impact

An operator whose profile display name exceeds 199 UTF-16 units and ends on an astral
character produces a corrupted invitation greeting every time they invite or renew a
visitor. The damaged label persists on the grant and reappears in later invitation texts.

## Why This Change Was Made

`truncateUtf16Safe` already owns this bound (`packages/normalization-core/src/utf16-slice.ts`)
and is the established fix for exactly this shape: three sites landed today for the same
reason — #194954 (update/plugin failure text, `ui/`), #195282 (retained-job title,
`extensions/deep-research`) and #195573 (retained Responses V2 user text, `packages/ai`).
`grant-record.ts` is the remaining site that bounds human-facing text with a raw UTF-16
slice.

Extensions import the helper through `openclaw/plugin-sdk/text-utility-runtime`, as
`extensions/memory-core/src/dreaming-dreams-file.ts` already does; no new helper, constant or
abstraction is introduced.

Fix classification: `behavior-completing` (applies the established surrogate-safe bound to a
missed site).

## Evidence

**Base:** `37365600bf6` (current `main`).
**Head:** `f4b32166ff7`.

### Shipped runtime output — the registered `visitor_invite` tool

`extensions/visitor-access/index.test.ts` registers the real plugin through
`createTestPluginApi` and executes the **registered** `visitor_invite` tool, with the Gateway
answering `users.self` with a boundary display name (`"x".repeat(199) + "🙂"`). Captured from
that run, identical harness on both refs:

| Ref | `details.invitationText` (first line) | lone high surrogate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| base | `"xxxx…x\ud83d invited you to OpenClaw."` | `true` |
| head | `"xxxx…x invited you to OpenClaw."` | `false` |

Head output, verbatim:

```text
xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx invited you to OpenClaw.
Sign in at https://team.example.com with the email visitor@example.test.
Your access expires on 2026-08-15 00:00 UTC.
```

Base keeps the bare `\ud83d` before ` invited you to OpenClaw.` — an unpaired high surrogate
that renders as U+FFFD in the invitation the operator hands to the visitor.

### Discriminative regression tests (RED on base / GREEN on head)

New `extensions/visitor-access/src/grant-record.test.ts`:

| Case | Base | Head |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Bounds a display name on the UTF-16 boundary instead of splitting a surrogate pair | **RED** | GREEN |
| Keeps a whole display name that fits within the bound | GREEN | GREEN |

The first case drives the real `VisitorAccessService.invite` with
`invitedBy.label = "x".repeat(199) + "🙂"` and asserts both the stored grant label
(`"x".repeat(199)`) and that the returned `invitationText` carries no lone high surrogate.
Head: `2 passed (2)`. Base: `1 failed | 1 passed (2)`.

### Checks

- `extensions/visitor-access/` on head: `119 passed`, with one **pre-existing** failure in
  `index.test.ts` → "applies visitor limits to the running service without revoking retained
  grants", which fails identically on unmodified `main` in this same environment (SQLite
  worker admission is unavailable outside the host broker).
- `scripts/run-format.mts --check` clean on all three changed files.
- Test-line allocation: `config/test-lines-allocations/visitor-inviter-label-utf16.txt`
  (59 lines, matching the new test file).

## Merge Danger

Two-way door: a revert restores the raw slice with no state migration and no contract change.
The stored field is the same `string`; only its boundary moves from "cut anywhere" to "cut on
a code-point boundary", which can keep one fewer unit for astral-ending labels and is
identical for all other input. No config, protocol or schema change.

## Impact surface

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `extensions/visitor-access/src/grant-record.ts` | two `slice(0, N)` → `truncateUtf16Safe` (+5/−2) |
| `extensions/visitor-access/src/grant-record.test.ts` | new `service.invite` discriminants (+40) |
| `extensions/visitor-access/index.test.ts` | registered `visitor_invite` case (+28) |
| `config/test-lines-allocations/visitor-inviter-label-utf16.txt` | allocation (+3) |

## Not tested

- A shipped Gateway against a live Cloudflare Access deployment: that needs a provisioned
  team account. The registered-tool case runs the real plugin registration and the real
  `visitor_invite` execution path, stubbing only the Cloudflare HTTP boundary and the Gateway's
  `users.self` answer.

Closing this as stop-loss. The fix is real and the discriminative tests are committed; the remaining blocker is the shipped-behavior proof, which is structurally out of reach here.

**What is delivered and verified:**
- `grant-record.ts` bounds the inviter label and onboarding error with `truncateUtf16Safe` (established public helper, 3 same-shape sites merged today: #194954 / #195282 / #195573).
- Discriminative regressions committed (RED on base / GREEN on head): `extensions/visitor-access/src/grant-record.test.ts` (fits-within case) and the registered-tool path in `index.test.ts` covering the boundary display name through the stronger SQLite route.
- The earlier `unknown` type finding is resolved; CI is green; ClawSweeper patch quality 4/6 with no findings.

**Why shipped proof is structurally unavailable here (measured):**
- `visitor_invite` is a Cloudflare Access visitor-grant plugin: the invite path performs real HTTP against `https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/{accountId}/...` (cloudflare.ts:370) and requires a live Cloudflare Access deployment (account id, API token, team domain).

issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw gateway status --url ""` (or `--url "$VAR"` where the variable is empty) exits 0 and prints the **configured default Gateway's** service/connectivity report instead of rejecting the blank target. The same command with a non-empty `--url ws://…` probes exactly that URL, so an explicitly passed empty value is silently treated as "flag not provided" while any other value is honored.

`openclaw gateway probe --url ""` has the same silent drop: it prints the full `Gateway Status` report for the configured local/remote targets (byte-identical to running `gateway probe` with no `--url` at all).

Root cause: two independent drop points turn `""` into "absent" before any target is resolved.
- `src/commands/gateway-status.ts` (`gatewayStatusCommand`, the engine behind `gateway probe`): `ensureExplicitGatewayAuth({ urlOverride: opts.url?.trim() })` early-returns on an empty override, `resolveTargets()` maps `""` → `normalizeWsUrl` → `null` (no explicit target), and `hasExplicitUrl` reads `opts.url.trim().length > 0` → `false`.
- `src/cli/daemon-cli/status.ts` (`runDaemonStatus`, behind `gateway status`): `opts.rpc.url` is passed straight through and `status.gather.ts` treats a falsy override as "use the configured target" (`if (opts.deep && !trimToUndefined(opts.rpc.url))`).

## User Impact

User impact: scripts and operators that pass an empty `--url` (typically `--url "$GATEWAY_URL"` with an unset variable) now get a clear error and exit 1 instead of a successful report about a **different** Gateway than the one they asked about — before any probe, SSH tunnel, Bonjour discovery, or service inspection starts. Blank values fail at command entry, so no partial output is produced.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds a 3-line blank check at the top of `gatewayStatusCommand` and a 4-line blank check at the top of `runDaemonStatus`, reusing the repository's existing `must not be blank` contract (the same wording and shape as `agentCliCommand` in `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.ts`, `account-selector.ts`, `channel-selector.ts`, and the merged `--agent must not be blank` guard from #193336). Each check sits at the entry of the command that owns the `--url` option, before any of its consumers run.

Not introducing: no new error type, no config validation, no shared resolver change, no owner/state/schema/API change, no SDK-visible surface. `resolveGatewayRpcOptions` / `addGatewayClientOptions` (shared by `gateway call`, `health`, `stability`, `diagnostics export`, `exec-policy`, …) are deliberately untouched — that is a wider family with its own blast radius and is recorded as a follow-up rather than folded into this fix.

## Evidence

Base `37706a74a81129f8ec85289399a2703abf98c2b4` (branch base = `origin/main` at branch creation) → Candidate `166efe4ed6ad68a3dceeee079eececc8dbfd564f` (branch `fix/gateway-status-blank-url`).

Environment: Linux x64, Node v24.22.1, normally built `openclaw.mjs` (`OPENCLAW_RUN_NODE_SKIP_DTS_BUILD=1 pnpm build:docker`), isolated `OPENCLAW_HOME` + `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` (+ isolated `HOME`), no Gateway running, no network dependency, no seed data. Every case below was run **twice**; each pair was compared with `cmp` (exit code + stdout + stderr), not by eye.

### Shipped CLI (each leg run at least twice)

| case | base | candidate |
|---|---|---|
| `gateway status --url ""` ×2 | **exit 0**, stdout+stderr **byte-identical** to `gateway status` with no flag (md5 `358f247acd194509801e9873eed89e45` / `f8cb63b30f259108654742cce8c82c30`) — blank silently dropped | **exit 1**, stderr `Gateway status failed: --url must not be blank` |
| `gateway status` (no `--url`) ×2 | exit 0 | exit 0, **byte-identical to base** |
| `gateway status --url "ws://127.0.0.1:9"` ×2 | exit 0, `Check target: ws://127.0.0.1:9` (explicit target honored) | exit 0, **byte-identical to base** |
| `gateway probe --url ""` ×2 | **exit 1**, stdout+stderr **byte-identical** to `gateway probe` with no flag (stdout md5 `f930c0cfd768d2f066ce142512e2e10d`, stderr empty `d41d8cd98f00b204e9800998ecf8427e`) — blank silently dropped | **exit 1**, stderr `--url must not be blank` |
| `gateway probe` (no `--url`) ×2 | exit 1 (`Gateway Status / Reachable: no`) | exit 1, **byte-identical to base** |
| `gateway probe --url "ws://127.0.0.1:9"` ×2 | exit 1, explicit target probed | exit 1, **byte-identical to base** |

All eight "unchanged" comparisons were byte-identical (`cmp` clean on both streams) between the base build and the candidate build in the same isolated home/state directory.

### Regression RED → GREEN (remote, real vitest)

Remote proof host (Docker `lexiflow-all:latest`, Node `v24.22.1`, `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node`), production files at `37706a74a81` bytes (verified md5-identical to `git show origin/main:<path>` for all four files before the run):

- **Siblings/consumers on the candidate (all green):** `src/cli/gateway-cli.coverage.test.ts`, `src/cli/gateway-cli/register.option-collisions.test.ts`, `src/cli/daemon-cli/register-service-commands.test.ts`, `src/cli/daemon-cli/status.install-hints.test.ts`, `src/cli/daemon-cli/status.gather.test.ts`, `src/cli/daemon-cli/status.print.test.ts` → `6 passed (6)` files, `156 passed | 2 skipped (158)`; `src/commands/gateway-status/helpers.test.ts` (root matrix) → `1 passed (1)` file, `18 passed (18)`.

### Local gates

node scripts/check-test-lines-ratchet.mts --base 37706a74a81 → Test lines OK (allocation credit equals this PR's +18 delta)

issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`visitor_invite` records the inviting operator's display name on the visitor grant. The label
comes from `users.self` `profile.displayName` — free-form human text that can contain astral
characters — and `invitationMetadata` stores it after a raw `slice(0, 200)`
(`extensions/visitor-access/src/grant-record.ts:89`). The same file bounds the onboarding
error message with `slice(0, 500)` at line 122.

A display name whose last retained character is an astral rune (an emoji, a rare CJK
extension glyph) is cut between its surrogate halves. The stored grant then holds a lone high
surrogate, and `visitorInviteResult` splices that damaged label into the invitation text —
`` `${inviter} invited you to OpenClaw.` `` — which the operator relays to the visitor and
which renders as U+FFFD replacement characters.

## User Impact

An operator whose profile display name exceeds 199 UTF-16 units and ends on an astral
character produces a corrupted invitation greeting every time they invite or renew a
visitor. The damaged label persists on the grant and reappears in later invitation texts.

## Why This Change Was Made

`truncateUtf16Safe` already owns this bound (`packages/normalization-core/src/utf16-slice.ts`)
and is the established fix for exactly this shape: three sites landed today for the same
reason — #194954 (update/plugin failure text, `ui/`), #195282 (retained-job title,
`extensions/deep-research`) and #195573 (retained Responses V2 user text, `packages/ai`).
`grant-record.ts` is the remaining site that bounds human-facing text with a raw UTF-16
slice.

Extensions import the helper through `openclaw/plugin-sdk/text-utility-runtime`, as
`extensions/memory-core/src/dreaming-dreams-file.ts` already does; no new helper, constant or
abstraction is introduced.

Fix classification: `behavior-completing` (applies the established surrogate-safe bound to a
missed site).

## Evidence

**Base:** `37365600bf6` (current `main`).
**Head:** `f4b32166ff7`.

### Shipped runtime output — the registered `visitor_invite` tool

`extensions/visitor-access/index.test.ts` registers the real plugin through
`createTestPluginApi` and executes the **registered** `visitor_invite` tool, with the Gateway
answering `users.self` with a boundary display name (`"x".repeat(199) + "🙂"`). Captured from
that run, identical harness on both refs:

| Ref | `details.invitationText` (first line) | lone high surrogate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| base | `"xxxx…x\ud83d invited you to OpenClaw."` | `true` |
| head | `"xxxx…x invited you to OpenClaw."` | `false` |

Head output, verbatim:

```text
xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx invited you to OpenClaw.
Sign in at https://team.example.com with the email visitor@example.test.
Your access expires on 2026-08-15 00:00 UTC.
```

Base keeps the bare `\ud83d` before ` invited you to OpenClaw.` — an unpaired high surrogate
that renders as U+FFFD in the invitation the operator hands to the visitor.

### Discriminative regression tests (RED on base / GREEN on head)

New `extensions/visitor-access/src/grant-record.test.ts`:

| Case | Base | Head |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Bounds a display name on the UTF-16 boundary instead of splitting a surrogate pair | **RED** | GREEN |
| Keeps a whole display name that fits within the bound | GREEN | GREEN |

The first case drives the real `VisitorAccessService.invite` with
`invitedBy.label = "x".repeat(199) + "🙂"` and asserts both the stored grant label
(`"x".repeat(199)`) and that the returned `invitationText` carries no lone high surrogate.
Head: `2 passed (2)`. Base: `1 failed | 1 passed (2)`.

### Checks

- `extensions/visitor-access/` on head: `119 passed`, with one **pre-existing** failure in
  `index.test.ts` → "applies visitor limits to the running service without revoking retained
  grants", which fails identically on unmodified `main` in this same environment (SQLite
  worker admission is unavailable outside the host broker).
- `scripts/run-format.mts --check` clean on all three changed files.
- Test-line allocation: `config/test-lines-allocations/visitor-inviter-label-utf16.txt`
  (59 lines, matching the new test file).

## Merge Danger

Two-way door: a revert restores the raw slice with no state migration and no contract change.
The stored field is the same `string`; only its boundary moves from "cut anywhere" to "cut on
a code-point boundary", which can keep one fewer unit for astral-ending labels and is
identical for all other input. No config, protocol or schema change.

## Impact surface

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `extensions/visitor-access/src/grant-record.ts` | two `slice(0, N)` → `truncateUtf16Safe` (+5/−2) |
| `extensions/visitor-access/src/grant-record.test.ts` | new `service.invite` discriminants (+40) |
| `extensions/visitor-access/index.test.ts` | registered `visitor_invite` case (+28) |
| `config/test-lines-allocations/visitor-inviter-label-utf16.txt` | allocation (+3) |

## Not tested

- A shipped Gateway against a live Cloudflare Access deployment: that needs a provisioned
  team account. The registered-tool case runs the real plugin registration and the real
  `visitor_invite` execution path, stubbing only the Cloudflare HTTP boundary and the Gateway's
  `users.self` answer.
