issue.title: fix(memory): expire embedding probe cache on elapsed time

labels.name: repo-535d150f
labels.description: Extension: memory-core

labels.name: repo-535d150f
labels.description: ClawSweeper judged the real behavior proof convincing.

labels.name: repo-535d150f
labels.description: Normal backlog priority with limited blast radius.

labels.name: repo-535d150f
labels.description: Very strong PR readiness with only minor maintainer review expected.

labels.name: repo-535d150f
labels.description: ClawSweeper has no concrete contributor-facing blocker left for this PR.

issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The memory plugin's embedding-availability probe cache is keyed on the wall clock. A backward wall-clock step (e.g. an NTP correction, laptop resume, or VM restore) makes `Date.now()` read *smaller* than the recorded `expireAtMs`, so the 30-second probe cache never lapses. The Gateway keeps serving the stale embedding-availability result until real wall time catches back up — long after its real window.

The sibling recall cache in `active-memory` moved from `Date.now()` to `performance.now()` in #193358, and the same cutover landed for the GitHub detail cache (#195450), Mantle discovery, and Nextcloud Talk room kinds (#193147). This embedding probe cache was left on the wall clock.

## Why This Change Was Made

`manager-provider-lifecycle.ts` writes `expireAtMs: checkedAtMs + EMBEDDING_PROBE_CACHE_TTL_MS` and reads `Date.now() >= cached.expireAtMs` with the same wall clock; `manager.ts` reads the inherited probe's `expireAtMs` the same way. All five sites move to `performance.now()` so the window measures elapsed time, not wall position. TTLs, probe policy, eviction and result data are unchanged.

The `primaryRecoveryRetryAt` window (same 30s budget) is the sibling wall-clock site in this file and moves together.

**Maintainer review update (085e01dcd31):** `checkedAtMs` and `cacheExpiresAtMs` are public wire fields in `doctor.memory.status` (clients read them as epoch dates). The cache entry now stores **both clocks**: `checkedAtMonoMs` (`performance.now()`) owns expiry, while `checkedAtMs` (`Date.now()`) stays a wall-clock epoch for the reported fields. The reader returns `cacheExpiresAtMs: checkedAtMs + TTL` so wire semantics are unchanged.

## User Impact

After a wall-clock rollback, a long-lived Gateway no longer keeps serving a stale embedding-availability probe (provider up/down, error reason) past its real 30-second window — the probe re-runs when its elapsed window actually elapses. Normal-clock behavior is unchanged. No new setting, error text, public SDK export, stored format, or migration.

## Evidence

**Red on base, green with the fix** (real `extension-database-workers` vitest shard, Node 24.22.1):

- **Base** (`7c7a4d5db4adf174b324cfe47c17123808a7de61`): new discriminant test fails — after the probe is cached, an elapsed `performance.now` step past the TTL with a backward wall-clock step still returns the cached result:
  ```text
  × memory index > expires cached embedding probe readiness on elapsed time even when the wall clock steps back
  ```
- **Candidate**: same file, 12 passed (12), including the discriminant test.

The discriminant test writes a probe, then pairs an elapsed `performance.now` (advanced past the 30s TTL) with a backward `Date.now` (an hour back) — a `Date.now`-keyed cache could never lapse under those reads, while the real elapsed window has already passed.

**Wire-semantics regression test (new in 085e01dcd31):** with `performance.now()` pinned at `7_000` and `Date.now()` pinned at `1_800_000_000_000`, the cached probe reports `checkedAtMs: 1_800_000_000_000` and `cacheExpiresAtMs: 1_800_000_000_000 + 30_000` (wall-clock epochs for clients), while expiry still follows the monotonic clock (non-null at `performance.now() == 7_001`). Full lifecycle suite: 23 passed (23) on remote Node 24.

### Pre-existing assertion adapted

The existing "caches embedding probe readiness across transient status managers" case asserted `cacheExpiresAtMs - checkedAtMs === 30_000` with exact equality. `performance.now()` returns a high-resolution float, so the same TTL arithmetic now yields `30000.000000000007`; the assertion moves to `toBeCloseTo(30_000)` with the behavior unchanged. All other existing cases pass unmodified (`manager-provider-lifecycle.test.ts` 12/12; `manager.borrowed-connection.test.ts` 22/22 covering the `manager.ts` inheritance read).

### Impact surface

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-provider-lifecycle.ts` | `checkedAtMs`/`nowMs` and `primaryRecoveryRetryAt` write+read move to `performance.now()` (−4/+4); dual-timestamp cache entry stores both clocks (+8/−4) |
| `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-registry.ts` | `MemoryEmbeddingProbeCacheEntry` gains `checkedAtMonoMs` (+4) |
| `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager.ts` | inherited-probe read moves to `performance.now()` (−1/+1) |
| `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-provider-lifecycle.test.ts` | discriminant test (+19) + wire-semantics test (+26) + existing equality → `toBeCloseTo` (−2/+2) |

Two-way door: a revert restores the wall-clock windows with no state migration or published-contract change. Blast radius is the process-local embedding probe cache only.

### Shipped Gateway proof

Real built Gateway (`runtime` dist) driven through the shipped operator RPC
`doctor.memory.status` with `openclaw gateway call`. Memory runs in its official
**FTS-only** mode (`memory.search.provider: "none"`), so no provider credential is
involved — the cache entry is produced and read by the same code this PR changes.

- `{"probe": true}` → `probeEmbeddingAvailability()` **writes** the cache
- `{"probe": false}` → `getCachedEmbeddingAvailability()` **reads** it and returns
  `checked` / `cached` / `checkedAtMs` / `cacheExpiresAtMs` on a hit

The backward step is applied **in-process** (a `--require` preload offsets
`Date.now()` after a trigger file appears); the host clock is never changed.

Sequence per run: prime with `probe:true` → roll `Date.now()` back one hour inside
the Gateway → wait **31 real seconds** (TTL 30 s) → `probe:false`.

| Build | Clock source in compiled `manager-runtime.js` | `embedding.checked` | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| head | `performance.now()` | **`false`** | expired on elapsed time ✅ |
| base | `Date.now()` | **`true`, `cached: true`** | stale probe still served ❌ |

Same collector, same RPC, same config, same FTS-only mode — the only difference is
the clock source, so the clock source is the cause of the cache not expiring.

Collector and both receipts (each recording the compiled-runtime sha256, the
priming response, the rollback offset, and the real start/end of the 31-second wait)
are on branch `proof/memory-probe-elapsed`:

https://github.com/wangmiao0668000666/openclaw/tree/proof/memory-probe-elapsed/proof-memory-probe-elapsed

## Precedent

Same cutover, already merged: #193358 (active-memory recall cache), #190894/#195450 (GitHub detail + preview), #193147 (Mantle / Nextcloud Talk). This completes the same elapsed-time sweep for the memory plugin's probe cache.

The sibling recall cache in `active-memory` moved from `Date.now()` to `performance.now()` in #193358, and the same cutover landed for the GitHub detail cache (#195450), Mantle discovery, and Nextcloud Talk room kinds (#193147). This embedding probe cache was left on the wall clock.

All five sites move to `performance.now()` so the window measures elapsed time, not wall position. TTLs, probe policy, eviction and result data are unchanged.

issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`visitor_invite` records the inviting operator's display name on the visitor grant. The label
comes from `users.self` `profile.displayName` — free-form human text that can contain astral
characters — and `invitationMetadata` stores it after a raw `slice(0, 200)`
(`extensions/visitor-access/src/grant-record.ts:89`). The same file bounds the onboarding
error message with `slice(0, 500)` at line 122.

A display name whose last retained character is an astral rune (an emoji, a rare CJK
extension glyph) is cut between its surrogate halves. The stored grant then holds a lone high
surrogate, and `visitorInviteResult` splices that damaged label into the invitation text —
`` `${inviter} invited you to OpenClaw.` `` — which the operator relays to the visitor and
which renders as U+FFFD replacement characters.

## User Impact

An operator whose profile display name exceeds 199 UTF-16 units and ends on an astral
character produces a corrupted invitation greeting every time they invite or renew a
visitor. The damaged label persists on the grant and reappears in later invitation texts.

## Why This Change Was Made

`truncateUtf16Safe` already owns this bound (`packages/normalization-core/src/utf16-slice.ts`)
and is the established fix for exactly this shape: three sites landed today for the same
reason — #194954 (update/plugin failure text, `ui/`), #195282 (retained-job title,
`extensions/deep-research`) and #195573 (retained Responses V2 user text, `packages/ai`).
`grant-record.ts` is the remaining site that bounds human-facing text with a raw UTF-16
slice.

Extensions import the helper through `openclaw/plugin-sdk/text-utility-runtime`, as
`extensions/memory-core/src/dreaming-dreams-file.ts` already does; no new helper, constant or
abstraction is introduced.

Fix classification: `behavior-completing` (applies the established surrogate-safe bound to a
missed site).

## Evidence

**Base:** `37365600bf6` (current `main`).
**Head:** `f4b32166ff7`.

### Shipped runtime output — the registered `visitor_invite` tool

`extensions/visitor-access/index.test.ts` registers the real plugin through
`createTestPluginApi` and executes the **registered** `visitor_invite` tool, with the Gateway
answering `users.self` with a boundary display name (`"x".repeat(199) + "🙂"`). Captured from
that run, identical harness on both refs:

| Ref | `details.invitationText` (first line) | lone high surrogate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| base | `"xxxx…x\ud83d invited you to OpenClaw."` | `true` |
| head | `"xxxx…x invited you to OpenClaw."` | `false` |

Head output, verbatim:

```text
xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx invited you to OpenClaw.
Sign in at https://team.example.com with the email visitor@example.test.
Your access expires on 2026-08-15 00:00 UTC.
```

Base keeps the bare `\ud83d` before ` invited you to OpenClaw.` — an unpaired high surrogate
that renders as U+FFFD in the invitation the operator hands to the visitor.

### Discriminative regression tests (RED on base / GREEN on head)

New `extensions/visitor-access/src/grant-record.test.ts`:

| Case | Base | Head |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Bounds a display name on the UTF-16 boundary instead of splitting a surrogate pair | **RED** | GREEN |
| Keeps a whole display name that fits within the bound | GREEN | GREEN |

The first case drives the real `VisitorAccessService.invite` with
`invitedBy.label = "x".repeat(199) + "🙂"` and asserts both the stored grant label
(`"x".repeat(199)`) and that the returned `invitationText` carries no lone high surrogate.
Head: `2 passed (2)`. Base: `1 failed | 1 passed (2)`.

### Checks

- `extensions/visitor-access/` on head: `119 passed`, with one **pre-existing** failure in
  `index.test.ts` → "applies visitor limits to the running service without revoking retained
  grants", which fails identically on unmodified `main` in this same environment (SQLite
  worker admission is unavailable outside the host broker).
- `scripts/run-format.mts --check` clean on all three changed files.
- Test-line allocation: `config/test-lines-allocations/visitor-inviter-label-utf16.txt`
  (59 lines, matching the new test file).

## Merge Danger

Two-way door: a revert restores the raw slice with no state migration and no contract change.
The stored field is the same `string`; only its boundary moves from "cut anywhere" to "cut on
a code-point boundary", which can keep one fewer unit for astral-ending labels and is
identical for all other input. No config, protocol or schema change.

## Impact surface

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `extensions/visitor-access/src/grant-record.ts` | two `slice(0, N)` → `truncateUtf16Safe` (+5/−2) |
| `extensions/visitor-access/src/grant-record.test.ts` | new `service.invite` discriminants (+40) |
| `extensions/visitor-access/index.test.ts` | registered `visitor_invite` case (+28) |
| `config/test-lines-allocations/visitor-inviter-label-utf16.txt` | allocation (+3) |

## Not tested

- A shipped Gateway against a live Cloudflare Access deployment: that needs a provisioned
  team account. The registered-tool case runs the real plugin registration and the real
  `visitor_invite` execution path, stubbing only the Cloudflare HTTP boundary and the Gateway's
  `users.self` answer.

issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Codex app-server keeps a process-local rate-limit snapshot per client, expiring it
after a 10-minute max-age window keyed on the **wall clock** (`Date.now()` in
`extensions/codex/src/app-server/rate-limit-cache.ts`). When the host wall clock steps
backward (an NTP correction, a suspended/resumed laptop, a Docker pause), the difference
`Date.now() - updatedAtMs` shrinks or goes negative, so the cached rate-limit payload is
treated as fresh **past its real 10-minute window** and is served to the UI and turn
context long after the quota state could have changed. Users and agents make decisions
(and see error copy) from stale rate-limit information.

## User Impact

Anyone running a Codex app-server whose wall clock is ever adjusted backward can see an
out-of-date rate-limit/credits/usage snapshot for longer than the intended 10 minutes.
The window only grows with the size of the backward step; a 1-hour correction extends
the stale window to over an hour.

## Why This Change Was Made

The repository-wide elapsed-time cutover #190894 already established that extensions use
`performance.now()` and keep wall-clock readings only where an epoch is part of an
existing contract. `updatedAtMs` here is a process-local write timestamp, never
serialized or exchanged, so it is not an epoch contract — this cache is a missed site
from that sweep. This matches the elapsed-cache repairs #193147 (Mantle discovery),
#195450 (GitHub detail reads) and #195472 (active-memory circuit breaker).

The GitHub detail reader explicitly keeps its 429 cooldown on the wall clock because it
must follow GitHub's own epoch (`x-ratelimit-reset`); this cache has no such epoch — the
rate-limit payload is a local snapshot whose age is purely a local comparison.

Fix classification: `behavior-completing` (extends the established elapsed-time contract
to the last wall-clock-keyed cache window in the codex app-server).

## Evidence

**Base (current `main`):** `712a3611f95` — `rate-limit-cache.ts` still uses `Date.now()`
in all three sites (verified: zero `performance.now()` in the file).
**Head:** `be53ca4dfef` (fix `0d65e8c9171` + shipped runtime probe `0c3108dfef9` + allocation + format polish).

### Discriminative regression tests (RED on base / GREEN on head)

`extensions/codex/src/app-server/rate-limit-cache.test.ts` — pairs an independent
`performance.now()` spy (advanced past the 10-minute window) with a `Date.now()` spy
stepped backward one hour, so a wall-clock-keyed window would never lapse while the real
elapsed window has already passed:

| Case | Base | Head |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Expires the cached read on elapsed time even when the wall clock steps back | **RED**: `expected { rateLimits… } to be undefined` | GREEN |
| Serves a fresh snapshot over the real client runtime until elapsed time passes despite a wall-clock step back | **RED**: same assertion | GREEN |
| Shares snapshots across module copies while isolating clients and expiring old reads | **RED** (spy moved to `performance.now`) | GREEN |

Head: `4 passed (4)`. Base: `3 failed | 1 passed (4)`.

### Shipped-flow probe — real client runtime + real notification path

The second discriminant drives the **real** `CodexAppServerClient` transport
(`createClientHarness`) and the **real** `ensureCodexAppServerClientRuntime` wiring: it
delivers a genuine `account/rateLimits/updated` codex app-server notification, which the
real runtime routes to the real `mergeCodexRateLimitsUpdate` in the real
`rate-limit-cache.ts` module (no module is mocked). Then the process wall clock steps
back one hour while the elapsed spy passes 10 minutes, and `readRecentCodexRateLimits`
must return `undefined` on head while base still serves the snapshot.

- Head: snapshot served fresh → expired after elapsed > 10 min despite the wall step.
- Base: `AssertionError: expected { rateLimits: { limitId: 'codex' } } to be undefined`.

Both refs run the identical test file; only `rate-limit-cache.ts` differs between them
(base md5 `3dfbf334cc4716d1b9e23dbd4ab83d87`, head `c624afd2e79d09d9d4c4d3a2678a0282`).

### Proof ceiling (named, measured)

A shipped-runtime proof of this cache requires the Codex app-server to actually serve
`account/rateLimits/read`, and `@openai/codex@0.164.0` refuses that without a live ChatGPT
subscription session. Measured on this host with the real bundled binary over stdio:

| Setup | `account/rateLimits/read` |
| --- | --- |
| No credentials | `-32600 "codex account authentication required to read rate limits"` |
| Synthetic `auth.json` (`stub-access` token) + `chatgpt_base_url` pointed at a local stub | same `-32600` — the request never reaches the stub (`/plugins/featured` was the only hit) |

The only shipped readers of this cache are `codex.accountUsage` →
`readCodexAppServerUsage` (`extensions/codex/src/account-usage-runtime.ts:75`) and the
usage-limit error path, both of which require an authenticated subscription profile
(`authRequirement: "subscription"`); neither has a credential-free shipped entry point
analogous to #195450's `controlUi.githubDetail` loopback stub. The clock comparison under
test is entirely process-local, so the real client runtime + real module is the deepest
boundary that a contributor without a live Codex subscription can exercise — this is the
same fixed ceiling as #193397 (msteams) and #193410 (imessage).

### Checks

- Consumers that import `rate-limit-cache` (`client-runtime`, `run-attempt-finalize`,
  `shared-client-usage`, `side-question`, `usage-limit-error`) keep their contracts;
  `rate-limit-cache.test.ts` + `client-runtime.test.ts` pass `31 passed (31)` on head.
- `scripts/run-format.mts --check` clean on the test file.
- Test-line allocation: `config/test-lines-allocations/codex-rate-limit-clock-elapsed.txt`
  (43 lines, matching the +44/−1 test diff).

## Merge Danger

Two-way door: a revert restores the wall-clock window with no state migration or
published-contract change. The cache is module-private (`defineCodexBuildState` + a
`WeakMap`), never persisted, serialized or exchanged; all three sites move together in
one closure. No config, protocol or schema change.

## Impact surface

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `extensions/codex/src/app-server/rate-limit-cache.ts` | three `Date.now()` → `performance.now()` (+3/−1) |
| `extensions/codex/src/app-server/rate-limit-cache.test.ts` | paired wall/elapsed discriminant + real-runtime shipped probe (+45/−1) |
| `config/test-lines-allocations/codex-rate-limit-clock-elapsed.txt` | allocation (+2) |

## Not tested

- A bundled `dist` codex run (local builds are banned on this host; the shipped probe
  runs the real client transport and real module sources under the repository vitest
  runtime).
- A credentialed upstream rate-limit stream: `@openai/codex@0.164.0` refuses
  `account/rateLimits/read` without a live subscription session (see *Proof ceiling*), so
  the probe injects a genuine app-server notification through the real runtime wiring
  instead. No live API account or credential was used.

issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

In the Control UI Settings form, the Enter that confirms an IME candidate in a secret field saved the half-typed value, and the rest of the composition was lost. WebKit's Enter right after composition end did the same. `handleHeldSecretKey` (`ui/src/components/config-form.secret-field.tsx`) had no composition guard.

## Why This Change Was Made

The secret field now uses the existing composition guard from `ui/src/lib/ime.ts`: `handleHeldSecretKey` ignores Enter and Escape while composing, and `secretInputProps` records `compositionend` so the bounded WebKit commit-Enter window applies. How secrets are stored, validated and sent is unchanged. `config-form.node.scalar.tsx` and `.oxlintrc.json` are unchanged.

## Evidence

Real Gateway in secretless Docker (node 24.22.1), built Control UI, Chromium composing through CDP in Settings > Automation > Webhook bearer token, fake values only. On main, Enter while composing sent `config.patch` with the partial value and the config stored it; with this change nothing was written during composition and the next Enter saved the full value. Enter right after composition end saved on main and is ignored here. Plain Enter, Escape, focus-out, the redacted placeholder and a non-secret field behave the same on both. Gzip: startup plus chat boot +0 B. Details and screenshots: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/195542#issuecomment-6734602089

Regression: the stored-secret save test in `ui/src/e2e/config-secret-field-save.e2e.test.ts` now presses Enter during a CDP composition before saving (fails on main). Test lines net 0.

backward (an NTP correction, a suspended/resumed laptop, a Docker pause), the difference
`Date.now() - updatedAtMs` shrinks or goes negative, so the cached rate-limit payload is
treated as fresh **past its real 10-minute window** and is served to the UI and turn
context long after the quota state could have changed. Users and agents make decisions
(and see error copy) from stale rate-limit information.

## User Impact

Anyone running a Codex app-server whose wall clock is ever adjusted backward can see an
out-of-date rate-limit/credits/usage snapshot for longer than the intended 10 minutes.
The window only grows with the size of the backward step; a 1-hour correction extends
the stale window to over an hour.

## Why This Change Was Made

The repository-wide elapsed-time cutover #190894 already established that extensions use
`performance.now()` and keep wall-clock readings only where an epoch is part of an
existing contract. `updatedAtMs` here is a process-local write timestamp, never
serialized or exchanged, so it is not an epoch contract — this cache is a missed site
from that sweep. This matches the elapsed-cache repairs #193147 (Mantle discovery),
#195450 (GitHub detail reads) and #195472 (active-memory circuit breaker).

The GitHub detail reader explicitly keeps its 429 cooldown on the wall clock because it
must follow GitHub's own epoch (`x-ratelimit-reset`); this cache has no such epoch — the
rate-limit payload is a local snapshot whose age is purely a local comparison.

Fix classification: `behavior-completing` (extends the established elapsed-time contract
to the last wall-clock-keyed cache window in the codex app-server).

## Evidence

**Base (current `main`):** `712a3611f95` — `rate-limit-cache.ts` still uses `Date.now()`
in all three sites (verified: zero `performance.now()` in the file).
**Head:** `be53ca4dfef` (fix `0d65e8c9171` + shipped runtime probe `0c3108dfef9` + allocation + format polish).

### Discriminative regression tests (RED on base / GREEN on head)

`extensions/codex/src/app-server/rate-limit-cache.test.ts` — pairs an independent
`performance.now()` spy (advanced past the 10-minute window) with a `Date.now()` spy
stepped backward one hour, so a wall-clock-keyed window would never lapse while the real
elapsed window has already passed:

| Case | Base | Head |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Expires the cached read on elapsed time even when the wall clock steps back | **RED**: `expected { rateLimits… } to be undefined` | GREEN |
| Serves a fresh snapshot over the real client runtime until elapsed time passes despite a wall-clock step back | **RED**: same assertion | GREEN |
| Shares snapshots across module copies while isolating clients and expiring old reads | **RED** (spy moved to `performance.now`) | GREEN |

Head: `4 passed (4)`. Base: `3 failed | 1 passed (4)`.

### Shipped-flow probe — real client runtime + real notification path

The second discriminant drives the **real** `CodexAppServerClient` transport
(`createClientHarness`) and the **real** `ensureCodexAppServerClientRuntime` wiring: it
delivers a genuine `account/rateLimits/updated` codex app-server notification, which the
real runtime routes to the real `mergeCodexRateLimitsUpdate` in the real
`rate-limit-cache.ts` module (no module is mocked). Then the process wall clock steps
back one hour while the elapsed spy passes 10 minutes, and `readRecentCodexRateLimits`
must return `undefined` on head while base still serves the snapshot.

- Head: snapshot served fresh → expired after elapsed > 10 min despite the wall step.
- Base: `AssertionError: expected { rateLimits: { limitId: 'codex' } } to be undefined`.

Both refs run the identical test file; only `rate-limit-cache.ts` differs between them
(base md5 `3dfbf334cc4716d1b9e23dbd4ab83d87`, head `c624afd2e79d09d9d4c4d3a2678a0282`).

### Proof ceiling (named, measured)

A shipped-runtime proof of this cache requires the Codex app-server to actually serve
`account/rateLimits/read`, and `@openai/codex@0.164.0` refuses that without a live ChatGPT
subscription session. Measured on this host with the real bundled binary over stdio:

| Setup | `account/rateLimits/read` |
| --- | --- |
| No credentials | `-32600 "codex account authentication required to read rate limits"` |
| Synthetic `auth.json` (`stub-access` token) + `chatgpt_base_url` pointed at a local stub | same `-32600` — the request never reaches the stub (`/plugins/featured` was the only hit) |

The only shipped readers of this cache are `codex.accountUsage` →
`readCodexAppServerUsage` (`extensions/codex/src/account-usage-runtime.ts:75`) and the
usage-limit error path, both of which require an authenticated subscription profile
(`authRequirement: "subscription"`); neither has a credential-free shipped entry point
analogous to #195450's `controlUi.githubDetail` loopback stub. The clock comparison under
test is entirely process-local, so the real client runtime + real module is the deepest
boundary that a contributor without a live Codex subscription can exercise — this is the
same fixed ceiling as #193397 (msteams) and #193410 (imessage).

### Checks

- Consumers that import `rate-limit-cache` (`client-runtime`, `run-attempt-finalize`,
  `shared-client-usage`, `side-question`, `usage-limit-error`) keep their contracts;
  `rate-limit-cache.test.ts` + `client-runtime.test.ts` pass `31 passed (31)` on head.
- `scripts/run-format.mts --check` clean on the test file.
- Test-line allocation: `config/test-lines-allocations/codex-rate-limit-clock-elapsed.txt`
  (43 lines, matching the +44/−1 test diff).

## Merge Danger

Two-way door: a revert restores the wall-clock window with no state migration or
published-contract change. The cache is module-private (`defineCodexBuildState` + a
`WeakMap`), never persisted, serialized or exchanged; all three sites move together in
one closure. No config, protocol or schema change.

## Impact surface

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `extensions/codex/src/app-server/rate-limit-cache.ts` | three `Date.now()` → `performance.now()` (+3/−1) |
| `extensions/codex/src/app-server/rate-limit-cache.test.ts` | paired wall/elapsed discriminant + real-runtime shipped probe (+45/−1) |
| `config/test-lines-allocations/codex-rate-limit-clock-elapsed.txt` | allocation (+2) |

## Not tested

- A bundled `dist` codex run (local builds are banned on this host; the shipped probe
  runs the real client transport and real module sources under the repository vitest
  runtime).
- A credentialed upstream rate-limit stream: `@openai/codex@0.164.0` refuses
  `account/rateLimits/read` without a live subscription session (see *Proof ceiling*), so
  the probe injects a genuine app-server notification through the real runtime wiring
  instead. No live API account or credential was used.

issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The GitHub detail reader (`controlUi.githubDetail`, `tools.github read`) caches issue/PR/commit documents in a process-local map keyed on the host wall clock. A `+5 min` correction expires every cached detail at once and re-issues the repository and item reads; a `−5 min` correction serves PR heads and check state well past their 30-second window.

## User Impact

After a laptop resume, NTP step or VM restore, a long-lived Gateway keeps serving cached details until their real 5 minutes / 30 seconds pass, instead of bursting fresh GitHub reads — and never serves an entry past its real window. Windows, LRU pruning and the GitHub-driven 429 cooldown are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`detailCache` is module-private: all three expiry writes and both freshness reads sit in one closure in `extensions/github/src/detail.ts`, and no entry leaves the module, so the five sites move to `performance.now()` together. This completes the elapsed-time cutover #190894 already made in the sibling `extensions/github/src/preview.ts`, and matches the elapsed-cache sweep #193147 for Mantle discovery and Nextcloud Talk room kinds.

The existing checks-expiry case drove the window with a `Date.now` spy only; it now advances both clocks so its ordering assertions hold either way. The checks-recovery regression in `detail-checks.test.ts` likewise advances the elapsed clock alongside its wall-clock spy.

Classification: `behavior-completing`. Production delta `+5/−5`; test delta `+24` with a scoped `github-detail-clock-elapsed` allocation.

## Evidence

- **Base** `54b059c478f` (current `main`) → **candidate** `db24c6c4669`.
- **RED on base** (current `main`, new tests applied): the elapsed-time discriminant fails because a backward wall-clock step keeps the `Date.now`-keyed cache alive past its real window:
  ```text
  × GitHub detail public read boundary > expires cached reads on elapsed time even when the wall clock steps back
  × GitHub detail public read boundary > expires cached visibility failures   (clock spy now drives performance.now)
  ```
- **GREEN on candidate**: `detail.test.ts` + `detail-checks.test.ts`, `62 passed (62)`. The discriminant pairs an independent `performance.now` spy (advanced 6 minutes) with a `Date.now` spy stepped backward 1 hour, so a `Date.now`-based cache would never lapse while the real elapsed window has already passed.
- **Real-entry matrix**: same shape proven in #192583 on identical bytes — a real exported read against a loopback HTTPS GitHub stub: `+600 s` step → base re-reads, candidate holds; `−600 s` step plus real elapsed seconds → base serves stale, candidate refreshes; control runs match request-for-request.
- **Shipped Gateway trace**: the same matrix through `src/index.ts gateway run` and the real `controlUi.githubDetail` WebSocket handler reproduced it identically (recorded on #192583).
- **Checks**: `git diff --check` clean; oxlint clean; `check:test-lines-ratchet` covered by the scoped `github-detail-clock-elapsed` allocation.

## Relation to #191210 / #192583

This branch carries the same fix as my earlier #191210 / #192583, which were closed because the automated review was held by its input scanner (a pre-existing URL fixture in `detail-checks.test.ts`, `role: base`), not by any finding in this change. The discriminant test here is rewritten with the paired wall/elapsed clock spies proven in #193147's Nextcloud Talk cases. Current `main` still has all five `Date.now` sites.

## Merge Danger

Two-way door: reverting restores the wall-clock windows with no state migration or published-contract change. Blast radius is the process-local GitHub detail cache only; the 429 cooldown that must follow GitHub's own epoch stays on wall clock by design.

issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Active Memory timeout circuit breaker measures its cooldown with the wall clock. A backward wall-clock adjustment (e.g. an NTP step) makes `Date.now() - lastTimeoutAt` negative, so the breaker never reopens after its real cooldown elapses and recall stays paused after repeated timeouts indefinitely.

The sibling recall cache in this same file moved from `Date.now()` to `performance.now()` in #193358; the timeout circuit breaker (read probe and recorded timestamp) was left on the wall clock.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use `performance.now()` for both the circuit breaker's recorded timeout and its cooldown probe, matching the recall cache expiry in `recall-state.ts`. TTLs, breaker policy, eviction limits and result data are unchanged.

A regression asserts the breaker reopens after the cooldown elapses even when the wall clock rolls back.

## User Impact

After consecutive recall timeouts, recall no longer stays disabled forever when the OS wall clock moves backward. Normal-clock behavior is unchanged. No new setting, error text, public SDK export, stored format, or migration.

## Evidence

Built real Gateway (`chat.send` through the real Active Memory hook) with `active-memory` + `memory-core` loaded from source, a deterministic 2s-delay local OpenAI-compatible fixture (recall times out at the configured 250ms; the main run completes), and a process-local clock rollback preload that moves only `Date/Date.now` backward 10 minutes in every Gateway thread (`performance.now` and timers stay real). Config: `circuitBreakerMaxTimeouts: 1`, `circuitBreakerCooldownMs: 60000`.

Both refs: send a message → recall times out (`done status=timeout elapsedMs=266`) → breaker opens → roll the process-local wall clock back 10 minutes → wait past the real 60s cooldown → send the identical question again.

| Ref | Wall-clock rollback + real elapsed > cooldown | Gateway log | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| main (`Date.now()`) | 110s after open | `active-memory: agent=main ... skipped (recall paused after consecutive timeouts)` | recall stays disabled forever — breaker never reopens |
| candidate (`performance.now()`) | 182s after open | `active-memory: agent=main ... done status=timeout elapsedMs=257` | recall re-runs and times out normally — breaker reopened |

The candidate re-runs a fresh recall (a new 250ms timeout), while main stays paused. Both lanes ran the same real `chat.send` path with the same fixture and clock rollback. No system-clock change; only process-local `Date` moved.

Focused discriminant test is red on frozen main (breaker stays open across the rollback) and green with the change.

## Merge Danger

Two-way door: process-local breaker state only; reverting requires no migration. Blast radius is Active Memory recall retry after timeouts, not persisted memory or other provider caches.

issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Pressing Enter to confirm an IME candidate (Chinese, Japanese, Korean input) in the
plugin credential secret input could save the literal draft before the user actually
submitted it. Two paths are affected:

1. A keydown with `isComposing: true` (or `keyCode 229`) reached the `onKeyDown`
   handler and committed the draft.
2. WebKit can deliver the committing Enter after `compositionend` with both composition
   flags cleared; that Enter also committed the draft.

## User Impact

Users entering credential literals in the Plugins page with an IME (most CJK users)
could have their partially-typed secret committed and sent to the Gateway
mid-composition, before they pressed Enter to actually submit. The draft is stored as
a literal credential value, so this both surprises the user and can persist an
unintended value.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared input-local IME guard (`ui/src/lib/ime.ts`, introduced in #177545) already
covers the browser toolbar (#194136), the skill library editor (#195356), the login
form, the command palette and the chat composer. The plugin credential editor was the
remaining secret input handling Enter without that protection. This applies the same
contract so a composing Enter is ignored and only a genuine submit (non-composing
Enter, blur, or Save) commits the draft.

Precedent: #194136, #195356 (same IME guard on other Enter-submitting fields);
#194436 (independently validated this exact credential-editor repair; closed without
merging after a proof request — this PR supplies the shipped proof and resolves the
conflict against current main).

Fix classification: `behavior-completing` (extends the established IME guard to the
last Enter-submitting credential input).

## Evidence

**Product head:** `8222f7b4217` (single clean fix commit, no proof files in the PR branch).
**Proof branch:** `proof/cred-editor-ime` @ `ee298d9eb72` (frozen collector + receipts + screenshots, outside the PR branch so the duplicate-scan stays clean).
**Base (current main):** `e673256f8a9351607912329020857906643a1c1c` — the credential
editor on main has no IME guard (confirmed: `ui/src/pages/plugins/credential-editor.tsx`
imports nothing from `lib/ime.ts`).

### Discriminative browser regression tests

`ui/src/pages/plugins/credential-editor.browser.test.tsx` (real Chromium) — three new
cases:

| Case | Base | Head |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Composing Enter (`isComposing: true`) does not commit | **RED**: `expected "vi.fn()" to not be called at all, but actually been called 1 times` | GREEN |
| WebKit post-compositionend Enter (grace window) does not commit | **RED**: same assertion | GREEN |
| Ordinary Enter after composition commits exactly once | — | GREEN |

Head: `27 passed (27)`.
Base: `2 failed | 25 skipped (27)`.

### Shipped proof — built Control UI + native Chromium CDP composition

Frozen collector `collector-cred-ime.mjs` (SHA256 pinned in `head-receipt.json`, both on the `proof/cred-editor-ime` branch: https://github.com/wangmiao0668000666/openclaw/blob/proof/cred-editor-ime/proof-cred-editor-ime/collector-cred-ime.mjs) drives the **built** production Control UI
(`vite build` → `dist/control-ui`, commit pinned, `dirty: false`) in **native Chromium**
via the official synthetic Gateway, opening the real Plugins → Workboard → Settings →
"Search API key" credential editor (`plugins.credentials.inspect` reports `missing`).

Native CDP `Input.imeSetComposition` starts a real browser composition; composing Enter
uses `Input.dispatchKeyEvent` (keyCode 229); the ordinary Enter is a genuine keyboard

| Ordinary Enter (positive control) | **+1** |
| Composing Enter during native composition | **0** (draft retained) |
| Commit composition, then ordinary Enter | **+1** |

on main. [`base-receipt.md`](https://github.com/wangmiao0668000666/openclaw/blob/proof/cred-editor-ime/proof-cred-editor-ime/base-receipt.md),
[`head-receipt.json`](https://github.com/wangmiao0668000666/openclaw/blob/proof/cred-editor-ime/proof-cred-editor-ime/head-receipt.json),
[screenshots](https://github.com/wangmiao0668000666/openclaw/tree/proof/cred-editor-ime/proof-cred-editor-ime).

- `oxfmt --check`: clean.
- Test-line allocation: `config/test-lines-allocations/credential-editor-ime-composition.txt`
  (33 added lines, matching the +33 test diff).

## Merge Danger

Two-way door: a revert fully restores prior Enter behavior. No migration, no new
persisted contract, no config change. The shared IME helper and the credential commit
path remain their existing owners; this only suppresses the composing-Enter commit.

issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The memory plugin's embedding-availability probe cache is keyed on the wall clock. A backward wall-clock step (e.g. an NTP correction, laptop resume, or VM restore) makes `Date.now()` read *smaller* than the recorded `expireAtMs`, so the 30-second probe cache never lapses. The Gateway keeps serving the stale embedding-availability result until real wall time catches back up — long after its real window.

The sibling recall cache in `active-memory` moved from `Date.now()` to `performance.now()` in #193358, and the same cutover landed for the GitHub detail cache (#195450), Mantle discovery, and Nextcloud Talk room kinds (#193147). This embedding probe cache was left on the wall clock.

## Why This Change Was Made

`manager-provider-lifecycle.ts` writes `expireAtMs: checkedAtMs + EMBEDDING_PROBE_CACHE_TTL_MS` and reads `Date.now() >= cached.expireAtMs` with the same wall clock; `manager.ts` reads the inherited probe's `expireAtMs` the same way. All five sites move to `performance.now()` so the window measures elapsed time, not wall position. TTLs, probe policy, eviction and result data are unchanged.

The `primaryRecoveryRetryAt` window (same 30s budget) is the sibling wall-clock site in this file and moves together.

**Maintainer review update (085e01dcd31):** `checkedAtMs` and `cacheExpiresAtMs` are public wire fields in `doctor.memory.status` (clients read them as epoch dates). The cache entry now stores **both clocks**: `checkedAtMonoMs` (`performance.now()`) owns expiry, while `checkedAtMs` (`Date.now()`) stays a wall-clock epoch for the reported fields. The reader returns `cacheExpiresAtMs: checkedAtMs + TTL` so wire semantics are unchanged.

## User Impact

After a wall-clock rollback, a long-lived Gateway no longer keeps serving a stale embedding-availability probe (provider up/down, error reason) past its real 30-second window — the probe re-runs when its elapsed window actually elapses. Normal-clock behavior is unchanged. No new setting, error text, public SDK export, stored format, or migration.

## Evidence

**Red on base, green with the fix** (real `extension-database-workers` vitest shard, Node 24.22.1):

- **Base** (`7c7a4d5db4adf174b324cfe47c17123808a7de61`): new discriminant test fails — after the probe is cached, an elapsed `performance.now` step past the TTL with a backward wall-clock step still returns the cached result:
  ```text
  × memory index > expires cached embedding probe readiness on elapsed time even when the wall clock steps back
  ```
- **Candidate**: same file, 12 passed (12), including the discriminant test.

The discriminant test writes a probe, then pairs an elapsed `performance.now` (advanced past the 30s TTL) with a backward `Date.now` (an hour back) — a `Date.now`-keyed cache could never lapse under those reads, while the real elapsed window has already passed.

**Wire-semantics regression test (new in 085e01dcd31):** with `performance.now()` pinned at `7_000` and `Date.now()` pinned at `1_800_000_000_000`, the cached probe reports `checkedAtMs: 1_800_000_000_000` and `cacheExpiresAtMs: 1_800_000_000_000 + 30_000` (wall-clock epochs for clients), while expiry still follows the monotonic clock (non-null at `performance.now() == 7_001`). Full lifecycle suite: 23 passed (23) on remote Node 24.

### Pre-existing assertion adapted

The existing "caches embedding probe readiness across transient status managers" case asserted `cacheExpiresAtMs - checkedAtMs === 30_000` with exact equality. `performance.now()` returns a high-resolution float, so the same TTL arithmetic now yields `30000.000000000007`; the assertion moves to `toBeCloseTo(30_000)` with the behavior unchanged. All other existing cases pass unmodified (`manager-provider-lifecycle.test.ts` 12/12; `manager.borrowed-connection.test.ts` 22/22 covering the `manager.ts` inheritance read).

### Impact surface

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-provider-lifecycle.ts` | `checkedAtMs`/`nowMs` and `primaryRecoveryRetryAt` write+read move to `performance.now()` (−4/+4); dual-timestamp cache entry stores both clocks (+8/−4) |
| `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-registry.ts` | `MemoryEmbeddingProbeCacheEntry` gains `checkedAtMonoMs` (+4) |
| `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager.ts` | inherited-probe read moves to `performance.now()` (−1/+1) |
| `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-provider-lifecycle.test.ts` | discriminant test (+19) + wire-semantics test (+26) + existing equality → `toBeCloseTo` (−2/+2) |

Two-way door: a revert restores the wall-clock windows with no state migration or published-contract change. Blast radius is the process-local embedding probe cache only.

### Shipped Gateway proof

Real built Gateway (`runtime` dist) driven through the shipped operator RPC
`doctor.memory.status` with `openclaw gateway call`. Memory runs in its official
**FTS-only** mode (`memory.search.provider: "none"`), so no provider credential is
involved — the cache entry is produced and read by the same code this PR changes.

- `{"probe": true}` → `probeEmbeddingAvailability()` **writes** the cache
- `{"probe": false}` → `getCachedEmbeddingAvailability()` **reads** it and returns
  `checked` / `cached` / `checkedAtMs` / `cacheExpiresAtMs` on a hit

The backward step is applied **in-process** (a `--require` preload offsets
`Date.now()` after a trigger file appears); the host clock is never changed.

Sequence per run: prime with `probe:true` → roll `Date.now()` back one hour inside
the Gateway → wait **31 real seconds** (TTL 30 s) → `probe:false`.

| Build | Clock source in compiled `manager-runtime.js` | `embedding.checked` | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| head | `performance.now()` | **`false`** | expired on elapsed time ✅ |
| base | `Date.now()` | **`true`, `cached: true`** | stale probe still served ❌ |

Same collector, same RPC, same config, same FTS-only mode — the only difference is
the clock source, so the clock source is the cause of the cache not expiring.

Collector and both receipts (each recording the compiled-runtime sha256, the
priming response, the rollback offset, and the real start/end of the 31-second wait)
are on branch `proof/memory-probe-elapsed`:

https://github.com/wangmiao0668000666/openclaw/tree/proof/memory-probe-elapsed/proof-memory-probe-elapsed

## Precedent

Same cutover, already merged: #193358 (active-memory recall cache), #190894/#195450 (GitHub detail + preview), #193147 (Mantle / Nextcloud Talk). This completes the same elapsed-time sweep for the memory plugin's probe cache.

Steer document rendering (`renderInboundDocumentContext` at `chat-send-input-dispatch.ts:522`) does not forward the active run's cancellation signal. ## User Impact

Interrupted steers cancel their in-flight document extraction promptly instead of leaving extraction running to completion. The repair forwards the same already-owned `activeRunAbort.controller.signal` that the surrounding admission path already uses for the run's abort signal.

## Why This Change Was Made

`renderInboundDocumentContext` already accepts an optional `signal` ("Cancels in-flight extraction") and threads it through `extractFileContext` into the attachment `getBuffer`/download cancellation path added by #194399. The call site was the only non-test caller that did not pass it. Forwarding the existing signal requires no new machinery — the abort controller is already in scope and already used for the late-reply abort signal at the same call site.

## Evidence

- Discriminating regression (remote, real test entry): the steer-document suite asserts the render mock receives an `AbortSignal` (mirroring #194399/#187438). On the unpatched production the steer-document case fails (133/134); with the one-line fix the suite passes 134/134. A control run with the assertion removed and unpatched production passes 134/134, confirming the failure is caused by the missing signal, not by the render-content assertions.

labels.name: repo-535d150f

labels.name: repo-535d150f

issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Active Memory timeout circuit breaker measures its cooldown with the wall clock. A backward wall-clock adjustment (e.g. an NTP step) makes `Date.now() - lastTimeoutAt` negative, so the breaker never reopens after its real cooldown elapses and recall stays paused after repeated timeouts indefinitely.

The sibling recall cache in this same file moved from `Date.now()` to `performance.now()` in #193358; the timeout circuit breaker (read probe and recorded timestamp) was left on the wall clock.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use `performance.now()` for both the circuit breaker's recorded timeout and its cooldown probe, matching the recall cache expiry in `recall-state.ts`. TTLs, breaker policy, eviction limits and result data are unchanged.

A regression asserts the breaker reopens after the cooldown elapses even when the wall clock rolls back.

## User Impact

After consecutive recall timeouts, recall no longer stays disabled forever when the OS wall clock moves backward. Normal-clock behavior is unchanged. No new setting, error text, public SDK export, stored format, or migration.

## Evidence

Built real Gateway (`chat.send` through the real Active Memory hook) with `active-memory` + `memory-core` loaded from source, a deterministic 2s-delay local OpenAI-compatible fixture (recall times out at the configured 250ms; the main run completes), and a process-local clock rollback preload that moves only `Date/Date.now` backward 10 minutes in every Gateway thread (`performance.now` and timers stay real). Config: `circuitBreakerMaxTimeouts: 1`, `circuitBreakerCooldownMs: 60000`.

Both refs: send a message → recall times out (`done status=timeout elapsedMs=266`) → breaker opens → roll the process-local wall clock back 10 minutes → wait past the real 60s cooldown → send the identical question again.

| Ref | Wall-clock rollback + real elapsed > cooldown | Gateway log | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| main (`Date.now()`) | 110s after open | `active-memory: agent=main ... skipped (recall paused after consecutive timeouts)` | recall stays disabled forever — breaker never reopens |
| candidate (`performance.now()`) | 182s after open | `active-memory: agent=main ... done status=timeout elapsedMs=257` | recall re-runs and times out normally — breaker reopened |

The candidate re-runs a fresh recall (a new 250ms timeout), while main stays paused. Both lanes ran the same real `chat.send` path with the same fixture and clock rollback. No system-clock change; only process-local `Date` moved.

Focused discriminant test is red on frozen main (breaker stays open across the rollback) and green with the change.

## Merge Danger

Two-way door: process-local breaker state only; reverting requires no migration. Blast radius is Active Memory recall retry after timeouts, not persisted memory or other provider caches.

issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Enter that confirms an IME candidate on the login form's Gateway URL or
secret field called `connect()` before the user finished composing, starting
a connection with a partially-typed value. CJK/IME users entering the
Gateway URL or secret (for example while an input method stays active) could
trigger a premature connect.

The login form is the last Enter-submitting text field in the Control UI
without the shared input-local IME guard: the chat composer, browser address,
skill editor, and plugin credentials already reuse `isComposingKeyboardEvent`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing input-local IME owner from #177545 (`ui/src/lib/ime.ts`):
`isComposingKeyboardEvent` recognizes active composition (`isComposing` or
`keyCode 229`) and the bounded WebKit commit-Enter grace after
`compositionend`; `recordCompositionEnd` / `clearCompositionEnd` retire the
marker on keyup and blur. This is the same pattern as the browser address
input (#194136) and the skill editor (#195356). No new timer, global state,
or controller API; URL normalization and connect behavior are unchanged.

Precedent: #194136, #195356 (same IME guard on other Enter-submitting fields).

## User Impact

IME users connecting to a Gateway no longer have a candidate-confirmation
Enter start a connection with an unfinished URL or secret. An intentional
Enter (after composition commits) still connects exactly as before; blur and
the Connect button are unchanged.

## Evidence

**Red on base, green with fix.**

Base: `826999cd5f76f4867a69869489a4fc51cd5e4a35` (upstream main CI ratchet base)
Head: `ea3b4ab8fb9ae7a6d533271f2ef76189d9c22686`

### Discriminative regression tests

- `ui/src/components/login-gate.test.ts` (jsdom): composing Enter
  (`isComposing: true`, `keyCode: 229`, and WebKit grace) on the URL and
  secret fields does not call `onConnect`; a later ordinary Enter does.
  - Base: `expected "vi.fn()" to not be called at all, but actually been called 1 times` (red)
  - Head: 21 passed (the single remaining failure, `explains setup codes`,
    is a local Node 24.13.1 `Uint8Array.fromBase64` limitation — CI runs
    Node 24.22.1 where the API exists; it fails identically on base).

### Native IME drive (real Chromium, CDP)

`startControlUiE2eServer` (source) + mock Gateway that rejects a stale token
→ the login gate shows its URL/secret fields. CDP `Input.imeSetComposition`
starts a native composition on the URL field:

- Composing Enter (`Input.dispatchKeyEvent`, keyCode 229):
  - Head: connect request count **unchanged** (delta 0).
- Commit composition (`Input.imeSetComposition` empty), then ordinary Enter:
  - Head: connect request count **+1** (normal connect still works).

The collector ran against the **built production Control UI** (`dist/control-ui`,
commit `97eba82c9321`, `dirty: false`) in native Chromium (`/usr/bin/google-chrome`,
headless). The synthetic Gateway recorded every `connect` request and rejected
the stale token with `AUTH_TOKEN_MISSING`. No live Gateway, session, credential,
or config was touched.

Receipt (`login-gate-ime-receipt.json`):

```json
{
  "status": "PASS",
  "positiveControl": { "delta": 1, "connectCount": 2 },
  "composingEnter":    { "delta": 0, "connectCount": 1 },
  "committedEnter":    { "delta": 1, "connectCount": 2 }
}
```

Screenshots of the login gate during the CDP probe (composing draft retained,
no navigation; error banner visible):

![Composing Enter retained draft](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wangmiao0668000666/openclaw/ea3b4ab8fb9ae7a6d533271f2ef76189d9c22686/login-gate-ime-composing-closeup.png)

![Composing Enter after keyCode 229](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wangmiao0668000666/openclaw/ea3b4ab8fb9ae7a6d533271f2ef76189d9c22686/login-gate-ime-after-closeup.png)

### Test-line budget

`config/test-lines-allocations/login-gate-ime-composition.txt` allocates the
39 added regression lines; `scripts/check-test-lines-ratchet.mts --base
826999cd5f76f4867a69869489a4fc51cd5e4a35 --no-merge-base` reports
`Test lines OK: 6586781; ceiling: 6586781; slack: 0` (the branch was
integrated with the CI ratchet base so the allocation exactly matches the
added lines; CI `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` passes).

### Impact surface

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `ui/src/components/login-gate-solid.tsx` | `submitOnEnter` guards with `isComposingKeyboardEvent`; both inputs add `onCompositionEnd`/`onKeyUp`/`onBlur` retirement (+10) |
| `ui/src/components/login-gate.test.ts` | two IME discriminative tests (+39) |

Two-way door: a revert fully restores prior Enter behavior. No migration, no
new persisted contract, no config change.

### Not tested

- Physical Japanese/Chinese IME hardware and WebKit/Safari (the shared IME
  owner's WebKit grace is covered by its existing consumers' tests; the
  CDP probe dispatches composing Enter on Chromium).

## Cleanup

All proof runs used the built Control UI with a mock Gateway (synthetic
stale token); no real Gateway, session, credential, or config was touched.
The CDP probe scripts were removed after capture.

issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The GitHub detail reader (`controlUi.githubDetail`, `tools.github read`) caches issue/PR/commit documents in a process-local map keyed on the host wall clock. A `+5 min` correction expires every cached detail at once and re-issues the repository and item reads; a `−5 min` correction serves PR heads and check state well past their 30-second window.

## User Impact

After a laptop resume, NTP step or VM restore, a long-lived Gateway keeps serving cached details until their real 5 minutes / 30 seconds pass, instead of bursting fresh GitHub reads — and never serves an entry past its real window. Windows, LRU pruning and the GitHub-driven 429 cooldown are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`detailCache` is module-private: all three expiry writes and both freshness reads sit in one closure in `extensions/github/src/detail.ts`, and no entry leaves the module, so the five sites move to `performance.now()` together. This completes the elapsed-time cutover #190894 already made in the sibling `extensions/github/src/preview.ts`, and matches the elapsed-cache sweep #193147 for Mantle discovery and Nextcloud Talk room kinds.

The existing checks-expiry case drove the window with a `Date.now` spy only; it now advances both clocks so its ordering assertions hold either way. The checks-recovery regression in `detail-checks.test.ts` likewise advances the elapsed clock alongside its wall-clock spy.

Classification: `behavior-completing`. Production delta `+5/−5`; test delta `+24` with a scoped `github-detail-clock-elapsed` allocation.

## Evidence

- **Base** `54b059c478f` (current `main`) → **candidate** `db24c6c4669`.
- **RED on base** (current `main`, new tests applied): the elapsed-time discriminant fails because a backward wall-clock step keeps the `Date.now`-keyed cache alive past its real window:
  ```text
  × GitHub detail public read boundary > expires cached reads on elapsed time even when the wall clock steps back
  × GitHub detail public read boundary > expires cached visibility failures   (clock spy now drives performance.now)
  ```
- **GREEN on candidate**: `detail.test.ts` + `detail-checks.test.ts`, `62 passed (62)`. The discriminant pairs an independent `performance.now` spy (advanced 6 minutes) with a `Date.now` spy stepped backward 1 hour, so a `Date.now`-based cache would never lapse while the real elapsed window has already passed.
- **Real-entry matrix**: same shape proven in #192583 on identical bytes — a real exported read against a loopback HTTPS GitHub stub: `+600 s` step → base re-reads, candidate holds; `−600 s` step plus real elapsed seconds → base serves stale, candidate refreshes; control runs match request-for-request.
- **Shipped Gateway trace**: the same matrix through `src/index.ts gateway run` and the real `controlUi.githubDetail` WebSocket handler reproduced it identically (recorded on #192583).
- **Checks**: `git diff --check` clean; oxlint clean; `check:test-lines-ratchet` covered by the scoped `github-detail-clock-elapsed` allocation.

## Relation to #191210 / #192583

This branch carries the same fix as my earlier #191210 / #192583, which were closed because the automated review was held by its input scanner (a pre-existing URL fixture in `detail-checks.test.ts`, `role: base`), not by any finding in this change. The discriminant test here is rewritten with the paired wall/elapsed clock spies proven in #193147's Nextcloud Talk cases. Current `main` still has all five `Date.now` sites.

## Merge Danger

Two-way door: reverting restores the wall-clock windows with no state migration or published-contract change. Blast radius is the process-local GitHub detail cache only; the 429 cooldown that must follow GitHub's own epoch stays on wall clock by design.

issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An acknowledged interrupt during the read-only `openclaw plugins marketplace list <source>` does not cancel the pending marketplace source read. When the source is a git/GitHub URL, the read is a `git clone` that stays open until the process is forced down, and an uncancelled late result can still reach the renderer. This is the invocation-interrupt class repaired for ClawHub package searches in #194076, and for inference in #192896 and #193893.

Precedent: #194076（同形状：read-only CLI 网络读 + invocation signal 转发；本 PR 换点位到 git-clone 泳道）

## Why This Change Was Made

#194076 forwarded the invocation signal through the ClawHub HTTP adapters (`fetchWithSsrFGuard` already declared `signal`). The marketplace list git-clone path was not covered: `runPluginMarketplaceListCommand` passed no signal into `listMarketplacePlugins` / `loadMarketplace` / `cloneMarketplaceRepo` / `acquireGitSource`, so the underlying `git clone` never saw cancellation even though `runCommandWithTimeout` already declares `signal`.

This PR preserves the established behavior: `runPluginMarketplaceListCommand` now checks the invocation signal before dispatch and before publishing a result, and forwards it through the existing chain into `acquireGitSource`, whose `run` closure passes it to `runCommandWithTimeout`. The parameter stays optional, so install callers (`installPluginFromMarketplace`, git-install, source-install) keep their existing behavior. No new validator, option, config, retry policy, lifetime owner, or schema.

Production LOC is `+17/-0`.

Classification: `behavior-completing`

## User Impact

Interrupting `openclaw plugins marketplace list <git-or-https-source>` inside a managed async-work scope now aborts the pending clone and suppresses the late result/output, instead of printing the marketplace after Ctrl+C. Uninterrupted listings, local path sources, and install flows are unchanged.

## Evidence

### Exact-head proof receipt

- Product head SHA: `02e423602de`
- Current-main RED baseline: `8662f3bf78dc7d644d207c8afb6f2f8b8f5750b0`
- Production entry: `runPluginMarketplaceListCommand` in `src/cli/plugins-marketplace-list-command.ts`
- Canonical owner exercised: `listMarketplacePlugins` in `src/plugins/marketplace.ts`, `acquireGitSource` in `src/infra/git-source.ts`
- Decision surface: the interruption signal forwarded from the CLI into the git-clone read path
- Recorder/readback boundary: captured CLI output / JSON write for a late marketplace result after the signal fires
- Acceptance RED: on pristine current-main, the same `AsyncWorkScope` scenario prints the late marketplace result (`writeJson`) after `beginClose()`; both cancel cases fail.
- Acceptance GREEN: on this head, both cancel cases emit no output, no JSON, no error, no exit; all 16 marketplace suite tests pass.
- Legal controls: uninterrupted json/text listing still prints the marketplace; existing marketplace/git-source suites (39 tests) pass unchanged.
- Cleanup and limitations: every run used isolated temp state; no production Gateway, session, channel, token, or config was touched.
- Format and ratchet: the cancellation regressions live in a dedicated command test file (oxfmt-clean), and the justified test lines are offset by a scoped test-lines allocation.

### Real Git child-process cancellation (RED -> GREEN)

The signal-forwarding contract is proven against a **real `git clone` subprocess**, not a mock. A local TCP listener that accepts but never responds (`git://127.0.0.1:<port>/repo.git`) holds a real `git clone` open; `acquireGitSource` calls the real `runCommandWithTimeout` and the real `git` binary. The CLI-side `AsyncWorkScope` owns the forwarded signal.

| Build | Interrupt | Returned after | Comment |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| RED (no signal passed) | — | **8041 ms** (timeout 8000) | clone hangs until `runCommandWithTimeout` force-kills it |
| GREEN (signal forwarded) | `beginClose()` | **11 ms** | git child process cancelled immediately; no late output |

Timing is monotonic wall time from start; both runs share the identical hanging source, temp output dir, and `git` binary. The RED run proves the pre-fix behavior waits out the whole timeout; the GREEN run proves the forwarded signal reaches and cancels the live git child process. No external network, credentials, or non-local services are involved.

### Shipped CLI real-PTY proof (independent build)

A **shipped `openclaw.mjs`** was independently built from this head (Node 24.22.1, tsdown runtime build) and driven through a **real controlling PTY** with a **real `git clone`** against a local slow git source (`http://127.0.0.1:19428/repo.git`, a TCP listener that accepts but never responds, so the clone stays pending). SIGINT is delivered as the terminal VINTR byte; the same slow source, temp HOME/profile, and `git` binary are used for every run.

| Build | SIGINT | Settled after | Observable behavior |
|---|---|---|---|
| RED (base, no signal) | VINTR | **1.6 s** | Bare `^C`; the process is hard-killed by the signal with **no cleanup notice and no cancellation of the in-flight clone**. Without SIGINT the clone stays pending past the `runCommandWithTimeout` window (>15 s, only the timeout force-kill settles it). |
| GREEN (this head, signal forwarded) | VINTR | **3.2 s** | `^CCommand interrupted by SIGINT. Waiting for cleanup before exiting.` then `{"ok":false,"error":{"type":"cli_error","message":"Plugin CLI invocation is closed"}}`; the live `git clone` child process is cancelled (zero git processes remain) and no marketplace JSON is emitted. |

The RED run proves the interrupted in-flight Git read is not cancelled on the base (either hard-killed with no settlement, or left pending to the timeout), and the GREEN run proves the forwarded invocation signal reaches the real `git clone` subprocess and cancels it with a clean settlement. No mocks are imported into the CLI; the built binary, the child git process, and the terminal are all real.


### Inspectable RED -> GREEN terminal trace (command suite)

`vitest run --config vitest.config.ts src/cli/plugins-marketplace-list-command.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`.

```text
RED (pristine main, production code without signal):
  × plugins marketplace list command > cancels the marketplace list read: before
  × plugins marketplace list command > cancels the marketplace list read: result
  Tests  2 failed (2)

GREEN (this head):
  ✓ plugins marketplace list command > cancels the marketplace list read: before
  ✓ plugins marketplace list command > cancels the marketplace list read: result
  Tests  2 passed (2)
```

### Test placement

The cancellation regressions live in a dedicated `src/cli/plugins-marketplace-list-command.test.ts` that mocks only `../runtime.js` and `../plugins/marketplace.js`, each with a `mock-isolation:` annotation accepted by the mock-exports guard:

- `pnpm check:test-mock-exports` — passes (two annotated factories in the new file).
- `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet` — passes; the added lines are offset by a scoped test-lines allocation.

The cancellation cases were deliberately kept out of `src/cli/plugins-cli.marketplace-entries.test.ts`, which carries a pre-existing redaction fixture with credential-like literals; touching that file changes its head blob and trips the review input scanner's literal-mismatch heuristic as a false positive.

### Verification

- `src/cli/plugins-marketplace-list-command.test.ts` — 2 passed (head), 2 failed (pristine base)
- `src/plugins/marketplace.test.ts` + `src/plugins/marketplace.sources.test.ts` + `src/infra/git-source.test.ts` — 39 passed (no regression)
- `pnpm check:test-mock-exports` + `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet` + `pnpm check:line-cap-ratchet` — pass
- `git diff --check`
- Not tested: a live `node openclaw.mjs` PTY run against a remote git URL on this host (network read; the terminal-recording form of this proof was supplied by the maintainer for the sibling #194076/#193893); the signal-forwarding contract is proven here at the live git-child boundary and at the CLI output-suppression boundary.

### Scope and risk

- Production LOC: `+17/-0`
- Test LOC: `+65/-18` (dedicated file; the entries suite is reverted to main)
- Existing-solutions preflight: reuses `getAsyncWorkSignal` (already exported for CLI commands) and the already-declared `signal` on `runCommandWithTimeout`; no new abstraction.
- Config/default, protocol/schema, authorization, storage, migration, upgrade impact: none. Optional parameter; all existing callers unchanged.

## What Problem This Solves

An acknowledged interrupt during the read-only `openclaw plugins marketplace list <source>` does not cancel the pending marketplace source read. When the source is a git/GitHub URL, the read is a `git clone` that stays open until the process is forced down, and an uncancelled late result can still reach the renderer. This is the invocation-interrupt class repaired for ClawHub package searches in #194076, and for inference in #192896 and #193893.

Precedent: #194076（同形状：read-only CLI 网络读 + invocation signal 转发；本 PR 换点位到 git-clone 泳道）

## Why This Change Was Made

#194076 forwarded the invocation signal through the ClawHub HTTP adapters (`fetchWithSsrFGuard` already declared `signal`). The marketplace list git-clone path was not covered: `runPluginMarketplaceListCommand` passed no signal into `listMarketplacePlugins` / `loadMarketplace` / `cloneMarketplaceRepo` / `acquireGitSource`, so the underlying `git clone` never saw cancellation even though `runCommandWithTimeout` already declares `signal`.

This PR preserves the established behavior: `runPluginMarketplaceListCommand` now checks the invocation signal before dispatch and before publishing a result, and forwards it through the existing chain into `acquireGitSource`, whose `run` closure passes it to `runCommandWithTimeout`. The parameter stays optional, so install callers (`installPluginFromMarketplace`, git-install, source-install) keep their existing behavior. No new validator, option, config, retry policy, lifetime owner, or schema.

Production LOC is `+17/-0`.

Classification: `behavior-completing`

## User Impact

Interrupting `openclaw plugins marketplace list <git-or-https-source>` inside a managed async-work scope now aborts the pending clone and suppresses the late result/output, instead of printing the marketplace after Ctrl+C.
